The University headquarters are situated in Paris, 5th district, at Place du Panthéon. The majority of law courses will take place at the Centre Assas, a campus in the heart of Paris, next to the Jardin du Luxembourg.

name: Université Paris Cité
description:
The Faculty of Law, Economics and Management is situated in the ’arrondissement’ called Malakoff which is situated approx 5 km from the centre of Paris.
The Faculty of Law is part of
the Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences
at the Université de Paris in total consisting of twelve components besides the Faculty of Law, Economics and Management.
Until the university merger in 2019, the university was previously called Université Paris Descartes.

name: Université Paris Dauphine
description:
Université de Paris Dauphine was founded in 1968. It is the only institution in France that is both considered a grande école and a university. Université Paris Dauphine-PSL offers multidisciplinary study programs for almost 9000 students. Located in the heart of Paris, Université Paris Dauphine-PSL offers an exciting environment with a vibrant campus life, which gives students the opportunity to participate in a wide range of activities. Courses are taught in English and French.
At the beginning of each semester, an intensive French seminar is offered for a fee.

name: University of Bordeaux
description:
The University of Bordeaux is one of France’s major public research universities, hosting over 54,000 students and approximately 6,000 staff members across multiple campuses. It is part of the Initiative of Excellence programme, which supports high-level research and international collaboration. The university is structured around several academic domains and maintains strong ties with national research organisations. Its scale and research output place it among the leading institutions in France, with a focus on interdisciplinary approaches and innovation. The university also participates in European university alliances, reinforcing its international engagement.
Bordeaux offers a distinctive setting for those interested in spending time in a region known for its cultural heritage, accessibility, and quality of life. The city is recognised for its architecture, riverfront developments, and active public spaces, and has been listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. It supports a wide range of exhibitions, concerts, and public events throughout the year, many of which are easily accessible to university students. Beyond the city, the surrounding region includes vineyards, Atlantic beaches, and natural parks, all within reach by public transport or short travel. This combination of urban life and regional diversity makes Bordeaux a practical and engaging base for an exchange semester.

name: University of Caen Normandy
description:
The University of Caen Normandy is a public multidisciplinary institution located in northwestern France. It hosts approximately 30,000 students and employs over 2,000 academic and administrative staff across several campuses in the region. The university is known for its long academic tradition, dating back to its founding in 1432, and for its commitment to research and international cooperation. It maintains partnerships with institutions across Europe and beyond, and supports a wide range of research activities through its laboratories and doctoral schools. Its structure allows for close interaction between students and faculty, and its regional focus contributes to a strong connection between academic work and local development.
Caen is a mid-sized city in the Normandy region, offering a combination of historical significance and modern infrastructure. Known for its role in World War II and its medieval heritage, the city also supports a vibrant cultural life, with museums, theatres, and public events throughout the year. Its location near the coast provides access to natural landscapes and outdoor activities, while its transport connections make it easy to reach Paris and other parts of France. For students considering an exchange semester, Caen offers a manageable and well-connected environment with opportunities to engage both academically and culturally.

name: University of Cergy-Pontoise
description: CY Cergy Paris University is a public university located in Cergy-Pontoise, France. The university was created from the merger of several schools of the University of Paris-Seine (ComUE), Cergy-Pontoise University and the École internationale des sciences du traitement de l'information – EISTI in 2020.

name: University of Lille
description:
The University of Lille is a major public institution in northern France, serving over 74,000 students and supported by more than 6,000 academic and administrative staff. It was formed through the merger of several universities and has since developed into one of the largest and most comprehensive higher education institutions in the country. The university is recognised for its strong research output, particularly in collaboration with national research organisations such as CNRS and INSERM. Its scale allows for a wide range of academic disciplines and research activities, while its regional engagement and international partnerships contribute to its role as a key centre for higher education in the Hauts-de-France region.
Located in the Hauts-de-France region near the Belgian border, Lille offers a strategic position in northwestern Europe. The city is a major transport hub, with high-speed rail connections to Paris, Brussels, London, and Amsterdam, making it accessible for travel and exploration during an exchange semester. Lille combines historical architecture with modern urban development and supports a wide range of cultural institutions, public events, and student services. Its active university community contributes to a lively academic atmosphere, while the surrounding region offers opportunities for both cultural engagement and outdoor activities. For students seeking a well-connected and academically diverse setting, Lille presents a practical and engaging option.

name: University of Montpellier
description: L’Université de Montpellier is characterised as an internationally recognized research-intensive university, with a history that dates back 8 centuries, yet committed to the key challenges of its time.

name: University of Pau
description:
The University of Pau and the Adour Region (UPPA) is a public multidisciplinary university located in southwestern France. It serves approximately 13,000 students and employs over 1,000 academic and administrative staff across several campuses, including Pau, Bayonne, Anglet, and Tarbes. UPPA is known for its regional engagement and its research activities in collaboration with national institutions such as CNRS and INRAE. The university places emphasis on environmental and societal challenges, and its structure supports close interaction between students and faculty. Its geographic spread and integration with local communities make it distinctive among French universities.
The city of Pau, where the main campus is located, offers a setting that combines access to the Pyrenees, proximity to the Atlantic coast, and a manageable urban scale. Pau is known for its historical architecture, public gardens, and views of the mountains, as well as its role in regional governance and education. The surrounding area includes opportunities for outdoor activities, cultural events, and cross-border travel to Spain. For students considering an exchange semester, UPPA provides a setting that supports both academic focus and regional exploration in a part of France that is less densely populated but well connected.

name: University of Perpignan
description:
The University of Perpignan Via Domitia (UPVD) is a public institution located in southern France, serving approximately 10,000 students and supported by around 900 academic and administrative staff. It offers a multidisciplinary academic environment and maintains active research centres in areas such as environmental science, law, and social sciences. The university is part of several regional and international networks and supports collaboration with institutions across Europe and the Mediterranean. Its relatively compact size allows for accessible student services and close interaction between students and faculty, contributing to a focused and supportive academic setting.
Perpignan is situated near the French-Spanish border, between the Pyrenees mountains and the Mediterranean Sea. The city offers a distinctive regional character shaped by Catalan heritage, with a walkable centre, active cultural calendar, and access to both coastal and inland landscapes. Its location makes it well suited for students interested in exploring southern France and nearby regions, with good transport links to cities such as Montpellier, Toulouse, and Barcelona. The combination of urban amenities and natural surroundings provides a balanced environment for study and everyday life during an exchange semester.

name: University of Strasbourg
description: The University of Strasbourg is a public research university located in Strasbourg, Alsace, France, with over 52,000 students. The French university traces its history to the earlier German-language Universität Straßburg, which was founded in 1538, and was divided in the 1970s into three separate institutions: Louis Pasteur University, Marc Bloch University, and Robert Schuman University. In 2009, the fusion of these three universities reconstituted a united University of Strasbourg.

name: University of Tours
description:
The University of Tours (Université de Tours) is a public institution located in the Centre-Val de Loire region, serving a student population of approximately 32,000 across seven faculties and several research units. It employs over 2,700 academic and administrative staff and supports a wide range of disciplinary and interdisciplinary research activities. The university is particularly engaged in regional development and maintains partnerships with national research organisations such as CNRS and INSERM. Its integration with local institutions and its role in supporting both scientific and cultural research give it a distinctive position among French universities, especially in terms of its regional impact and accessibility.
Tours is a mid-sized city situated along the Loire River, known for its historical architecture, public gardens, and role as a gateway to the Loire Valley. The city offers a balanced environment for student life, with cultural events, libraries, and public transport well integrated into the urban landscape. Its location provides access to nearby castles, vineyards, and natural areas, making it a practical base for regional exploration. Tours is also well connected by rail to Paris and other major cities, offering convenience for travel during an exchange semester. For students seeking a manageable and culturally rich setting, the University of Tours presents a well-rounded option.

name: Bielefeld University
description:
Bielefeld University, established in 1969, is a modern and research-driven institution with around 24,500 students and 14 faculties covering the humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, engineering, and medicine. It is known for its interdisciplinary approach and emphasis on unifying research and teaching. The university hosts several renowned research centers and institutes, such as the Center for Interdisciplinary Research and the Cluster of Excellence Cognitive Interaction Technology. Bielefeld’s innovative structure, including its central building where all faculties are under one roof, fosters collaboration and a strong academic community.
Located in the city of Bielefeld in the North Rhine-Westphalia region of Germany, the university offers a balanced student experience with both urban and natural surroundings. The campus is situated near the Teutoburg Forest, offering opportunities for outdoor recreation, while the city itself provides cultural venues, cafés, and student-friendly events. With an efficient public transport system and a welcoming atmosphere, Bielefeld is an ideal setting for exchange students looking for a mix of academic excellence and everyday livability.

name: Freie Universität Berlin
description:
Freie Universität Berlin, established in 1948, is one of Germany’s top research universities and a member of the German Excellence Strategy. It has around 33,900 students, including a large international community, and offers over 150 degree programs across the humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, and life sciences. The university is known for its strong interdisciplinary approach and global partnerships, with over 400 Erasmus+ agreements and numerous collaborations worldwide. Research is a central part of its mission, supported by institutes like the Otto Suhr Institute for Political Science and the Dahlem Research School for doctoral training.
Located in the green and residential district of Dahlem in southwest Berlin, the university offers a peaceful academic setting with easy access to the city’s vibrant culture and public transportation. Students can explore Berlin’s rich history, diverse neighborhoods, and thriving arts and cultural scenes while studying at a campus known for its modern facilities and international outlook. The city’s dynamic atmosphere, combined with Freie Universität’s strong academic reputation, makes it an attractive destination for exchange students.

name: Friedrich Schiller University Jena
description:
Friedrich Schiller University Jena is one of Germany’s oldest universities, founded in 1558, and today serves a student body of around 18,000 supported by approximately 4,500 staff members. It is a comprehensive public research university with a strong emphasis on interdisciplinary collaboration and international engagement. The university is known for its contributions to the natural sciences, humanities, and social sciences, and maintains close ties with major research institutions such as the Max Planck and Leibniz Institutes. Its compact structure and integration with the city allow for close interaction between students, faculty, and researchers, creating a cohesive academic environment.
The university is located in Jena, a mid-sized city in the federal state of Thuringia. Jena is known for its concentration of research institutions and its role as a centre for science and education in central Germany. The city offers a manageable scale, efficient public transport, and access to cultural and recreational activities, including hiking in the surrounding hills and visits to historical sites. Its location provides good connections to other German cities such as Leipzig, Erfurt, and Berlin. For students considering an exchange semester, Jena offers a setting that combines academic focus with opportunities for regional exploration and everyday convenience.

name: Goethe University Frankfurt
description:
Goethe Universität Frankfurt am Main is one of Germany’s leading research universities, known for its strong academic tradition and international orientation. Founded in 1914, the university offers a wide range of disciplines across its 16 faculties, with particular strengths in economics, law, social sciences, and natural sciences. It is home to several prestigious research institutes and maintains close ties with the city’s financial and cultural institutions. With a student population of over 45,000, including a significant number of international students, Goethe University fosters a vibrant and diverse academic community. Its commitment to interdisciplinary research and critical inquiry makes it an attractive destination for students seeking a rigorous and globally connected exchange experience.
Situated in Frankfurt am Main, Germany’s financial capital and one of Europe’s most cosmopolitan cities, Goethe University offers students a dynamic urban environment rich in professional and cultural opportunities. Frankfurt is known for its impressive skyline, international institutions, and thriving arts scene. The city combines modern infrastructure with historical charm, offering easy access to museums, theaters, and green spaces along the River Main. Its central location in Europe also makes it an ideal base for travel and exploration. For students looking to combine academic excellence with the experience of living in a global metropolis, Goethe Universität Frankfurt am Main presents an outstanding choice for an exchange semester.

name: Heidelberg University
description:
Established in 1386, the University of Heidelberg holds the distinction of being the oldest university in Germany, embodying a legacy of knowledge and intellectual pursuit that spans centuries. With a community of over 31,000 students, including approximately 6,000 international students, it provides a vibrant and inclusive environment for higher education. Nestled by the picturesque lake Neckar, the campus offers a serene and inspiring backdrop for academic pursuits, fostering a conducive atmosphere for learning and personal growth.
Recognized as one of the strongest research universities in Europe, the institution boasts 12 faculties encompassing a diverse range of disciplines. These faculties, such as Biosciences, Chemistry and Earth Sciences, Mathematics and Computer Science, Physics and Astronomy, Philosophy, Modern Languages, Theology, Law, Economics and Social Sciences, Behavioral and Cultural Studies, and Medicine, offer comprehensive academic programs that cater to a wide array of interests and career paths. Through a commitment to rigorous research and innovation, the university cultivates an environment that fuels intellectual curiosity and advances knowledge in various fields.
Heidelberg is a compact and picturesque city located along the Neckar River in southwestern Germany. Known for its Baroque architecture, cobblestone streets, and vibrant cultural life, the city offers a student-friendly environment with efficient public transport and a strong cycling culture. The city’s historic center is home to cafés, bookstores, and cultural venues, all within walking distance of the university. A fun fact: tucked inside Heidelberg Castle is the world’s largest wine barrel, the Heidelberg Tun, built in 1751 with a capacity of over 219,000 liters—though it was only filled three times due to persistent leaks.

name: Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin
description:
Humboldt University of Berlin is a public research university in the central borough of Mitte in Berlin, Germany. It was established by Frederick William III on the initiative of Wilhelm von Humboldt, Johann Gottlieb Fichte and Friedrich Ernst Daniel Schleiermacher as the University of Berlin (Universität zu Berlin) in 1809, and opened in 1810, making it the oldest of Berlin's four universities.
HU is divided into nine faculties, including its medical school shared with the Free University of Berlin, has a student enrollment of around 33,000 students, and offers degree programmes in some 189 disciplines from undergraduate to postdoctorate level.
Past and present faculty and notable alumni include an impressive 57 Nobel Prize laureates as well as eminent philosophers, sociologists, artists, lawyers, politicians, mathematicians, scientists, and Heads of State; among them are Albert Einstein, Karl Marx, Friedrich Engels, Otto von Bismarck, W. E. B. Du Bois, Angela Davis, Arthur Schopenhauer, Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel, Walter Benjamin, Max Weber, Georg Simmel, Karl Liebknecht, Ernst Cassirer, Heinrich Heine, Max Planck, and the Brothers Grimm.

name: Leipzig University
description:
Leipzig University was founded in 1409, making it one of the oldest in Germany: a comprehensive university with 14 faculties, 460 professorships and over 30,000 students. At 59 per cent, the proportion of female students is above average. Approximately twelve per cent of students are from abroad.
Around 50 Nobel laureates have worked, taught, or published their works here. In addition, important figures such as Johann Wolfgang Goethe, Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz, Friedrich Nietzsche, Richard Wagner and the German Chancellor, Angela Merkel, all studied here.

name: Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München (LMU)
description:
Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München (LMU Munich) is one of Europe’s foremost research universities, with a legacy of academic excellence dating back to its founding in 1472. LMU offers a broad spectrum of disciplines, ranging from the humanities and social sciences to medicine and natural sciences, and is consistently ranked among the top universities in Germany and internationally. Its programs are deeply rooted in cutting-edge research, and students benefit from close interaction with leading scholars and access to world-class facilities. With a strong international profile and a student body of over 50,000, LMU provides a stimulating academic environment that encourages intellectual curiosity and interdisciplinary collaboration.
Located in the heart of Munich, LMU offers students the opportunity to study in one of Germany’s most attractive and culturally rich cities. Munich is known for its high quality of life, vibrant arts scene, and proximity to the Alps, making it an ideal setting for both academic and personal growth. The city combines historic charm with modern innovation, and students can enjoy everything from museums and music festivals to outdoor activities and international cuisine. An exchange semester at LMU Munich promises not only academic enrichment but also a rewarding experience in one of Europe’s most welcoming and dynamic urban environments.

name: Osnabrück University
description:
Osnabrück University is a mid-sized public university in northwestern Germany, with a student population of around 14,000 and a staff of approximately 1,200 academic employees. It is known for its interdisciplinary research and strong collaboration between faculties, particularly in the humanities, social sciences, and natural sciences. The university places a strong emphasis on international cooperation and offers a welcoming environment for exchange students. One of its distinctive features is the close integration of research and teaching, supported by a compact campus structure that fosters interaction across disciplines.
The university is located in the city of Osnabrück, a historic and student-friendly city in Lower Saxony. With a population of just over 160,000, Osnabrück offers a manageable and affordable urban environment, while still providing a rich cultural life, green surroundings, and good public transport. The city has a strong academic and youthful character, shaped in part by its university community. Its location between the Teutoburg Forest and the Wiehen Hills also makes it attractive for students who enjoy outdoor activities alongside their studies.

name: RWTH Aachen University
description:
RWTH Aachen University (Rheinisch-Westfälische Technische Hochschule Aachen) is the largest university of technology in Germany and one of the most renowned in Europe. Every year, numerous international students and scientists come to the university to benefit from its high quality courses and excellent facilities, both of which are recognised at an international level.
With its 260 institutes in nine faculties, RWTH Aachen is among the leading European scientific and research institutions. More than 45.000 students are enrolled in RWTH, including over 11,000 international students from more than 120 countries.

name: Technical University of Munich
description:
15 academic departments. 42,705 students. 594 professors. 378,6 mio. Euros in third-party research funding. 17 Nobel Prize winners. The Technical University of Munich (TUM) is one of Europe’s top universities, and ever since its founding in 1868, it has been at the forefront of innovation. TUM spans several large sites in Bavaria: Munich, Garching, Weihenstephan and Straubing. These are home to the TUM Schools and Departments and the university's most important research facilities.
TUM has concentrated its expertise in life sciences in the TUM School of Life Sciences at the green and modern Weihenstephan campus. It is located on the outskirts of Freising and has evolved from the traditional disciplines of agricultural and life sciences.

name: TU Dortmund University
description:
TU Dortmund University is a forward-looking institution that combines strong academic foundations with innovative research across a wide range of disciplines. Established over 50 years ago, the university has developed a distinctive profile with 17 departments spanning engineering, natural sciences, social sciences, and cultural studies. With approximately 30,000 students and a dedicated faculty of over 300 professors, TU Dortmund fosters a collaborative and interdisciplinary academic environment. The Department of Social Sciences, founded in 2020, is particularly notable for its integration of sociological research, didactics, and the Social Research Center (sfs), making it an exciting destination for students interested in contemporary societal challenges and applied research.
Located in the Ruhr region, TU Dortmund offers students the chance to study in one of Germany’s most dynamic and evolving urban areas. Dortmund is a city with a rich industrial heritage that has successfully transformed into a center for technology, culture, and education. Students benefit from a lively cultural scene, green spaces, and a welcoming atmosphere, all within reach of major cities like Düsseldorf and Cologne. The university’s campus is well-connected and designed to support both academic and social life, making it an ideal setting for exchange students seeking a balanced and enriching experience in Germany.

name: Universität Hamburg
description:
The University of Hamburg is one of Germany’s largest and most diverse universities, with around 43,000 students and over 5,000 academic staff. It is a leading institution in northern Germany for both research and teaching, and is part of the German Excellence Strategy. The university is known for its strong interdisciplinary approach and its commitment to sustainability and social responsibility. With more than 180 degree programs and a wide range of research centers, it offers students access to a broad academic environment. A defining feature of the University of Hamburg is its close integration with major research institutions in the region, including several Max Planck and Helmholtz institutes.
Situated in Germany’s second-largest city, the University of Hamburg offers students the chance to live in a vibrant, international urban setting. Hamburg is a major port city with a strong cultural scene, a dynamic economy, and a high standard of living. Its many parks, waterways, and neighborhoods provide a varied and accessible environment for student life. The city is well-connected by public transport and offers a wide range of activities outside the classroom, from music and art to sports and volunteering. For students looking to combine academic development with urban exploration, Hamburg presents a compelling option.

name: University of Bayreuth
description: After the decision for its founding in 1972, the University of Bayreuth began teaching and studying in 1975. The University of Bayreuth has about 13,300 students and 1,650 academic staff (260 of them professors) on the campus in Bayreuth and at satellite campus in Kulmbach. This makes it one of the largest employers in the region. The university is located in Bayreuth, an 800-year-old city in the north of Bavaria, home to 73,000 residents

name: University of Cologne
description:
The University of Cologne is a university in Cologne, Germany. It was the sixth university to be established in Central Europe and, although it closed in 1798 before being re-established in 1919, it is now one of the largest universities in Germany with more than 48000 students.
Due to its outstanding scientific achievements and the high quality and diversity of its degree programs, it enjoys an excellent international reputation.

name: University of Freiburg
description:
The University of Freiburg, officially known as Albert-Ludwigs-Universität Freiburg, is one of Germany’s oldest and most respected universities, founded in 1457. It currently hosts around 24,000 students and employs over 8,000 staff nad almost 5,000 doctoral candidates across eleven faculties. The university is recognized for its strong research output, particularly in the life sciences, humanities, and sustainability studies, and is part of the German Excellence Strategy. A defining feature of Freiburg is its close collaboration with external research institutions such as the Fraunhofer and Max Planck Societies, offering students access to a broad academic network and research opportunities beyond the university itself.
Situated in the southwest of Germany near the borders of France and Switzerland, Freiburg is a vibrant university town known for its compact layout, green surroundings, and active student life. The city has a population of about 230,000 and is often cited as one of Germany’s most environmentally conscious and bicycle-friendly cities. Freiburg’s location at the edge of the Black Forest provides easy access to hiking, skiing, and other outdoor activities, making it an attractive destination for students seeking both academic engagement and recreational opportunities. Its international atmosphere and strong local support for education contribute to a welcoming environment for exchange students.

name: University of Göttingen
description:
The University of Göttingen, officially Georg-August-Universität Göttingen, is a research-oriented public university with a strong international reputation, particularly in the natural sciences and humanities. Founded in 1737, it currently enrolls around 30,000 students and employs over 4,000 academic staff. The university is part of several major research networks and maintains close ties with institutions such as the Max Planck Society, which has multiple institutes located in Göttingen. A notable feature of the university is its emphasis on academic freedom and its long-standing tradition of fostering critical thinking and interdisciplinary collaboration.
Göttingen seems to pulsate with a thirst for knowledge. It is a city shaped by students and academic life more than anywhere else in Germany. A total of 44 Nobel laureates are associated with Göttingen. Some were born in the city, while others came here to study, teach or conduct research. Göttingen is a compact university town in central Germany, with a population of approximately 120,000. Known as the "City of Knowledge", the city’s identity is closely tied to its academic community, and students make up a significant portion of the population. This creates a lively and student-focused atmosphere, with a wide range of cultural events, cafés, and public spaces geared toward young people. Göttingen’s location offers easy access to other major cities such as Hanover and Kassel, while its green surroundings and historical architecture provide a pleasant environment for study and daily life. The city’s manageable size and strong support for student initiatives make it particularly welcoming for exchange students.

name: University of Hohenheim
description:
The University of Hohenheim was founded in 1818.
The current profile of the University is unique due to the combination of its three faculties (Agricultural as well as Natural and Business, Economics and Social Sciences). Today, the University of Hohenheim is an internationally oriented campus university focused on cooperation and research.
The University of Hohenheim is located just 10 kilometers south of Stuttgart and less than 10 minutes’ drive from Stuttgart Airport.

name: University of Konstanz
description:
Since its foundation in 1966, the University of Konstanz has distinguished itself through its top-level research, excellence in teaching and studies, internationality and interdisciplinary collaboration. The University of Konstanz is comprised of thirteen departments that are divided into three faculties: the Faculty of Sciences, the Faculty of Humanities and the Faculty of Politics - Law - Economics.
At the international level, the University of Konstanz advances select and sustainable partnerships with over 70 research-focused universities in order to promote scientific collaboration and student exchange.

name: University of Mannheim
description:
The University of Mannheim is one of the leading higher educational institutions in Germany. This has been confirmed by numerous rankings, awards, by surveys among employers and by the German Excellence Initiative. The university's profile is shaped by its emphasis on business administration, economics, and social sciences.
Staff members at six schools and departments teach and carry out research in Business Administration, Economics, the Humanities, Social Sciences, Law and Business Informatics and Mathematics.
University of Mannheim has 12,000 students. The campus has an international and diverse student population with over 2,000 international students. Most lecture halls are inside the Schloss, one of the largest baroque buildings in the world. The campus is within walking distance from the city center.

name: University of Münster
description: The University of Münster is one of the largest universities in Germany with a rich and time-honoured tradition. It enjoys an outstanding reputation in the region and far beyond. Fifteen faculties with 120 degree programmes and some 30 research centres comprise the institutional backbone of the University. Some 45,700 students and 5,300 academics appreciate the University's excellent research opportunities, high-quality teaching, promotion of junior researchers, and the advantages of living in the city of Münster. Our slogan sums it up best: "living.knowledge".

name: University of Potsdam
description:
Since its founding in 1991, the University of Potsdam has excelled in research and teaching. With more than 20,000 students and seven faculties, the University of Potsdam is the biggest university in the Federal State of Brandenburg. It has four campuses.
The University of Potsdam is an international community with many faces and stories. Its international atmosphere is created by its students from all parts of the world, who decide to study in Potsdam - as well as by the internationally experienced professors and lecturers.

name: University of Rostock
description:
The University of Rostock is one of the oldest universities in Germany, founded in 1419, and has maintained a strong academic tradition for over six centuries. With around 13,000 students and a compact campus structure, the university offers a focused and accessible academic environment. It is organized into several faculties and places particular emphasis on interdisciplinary cooperation and international exchange. The university’s long history and its role in shaping intellectual life in northern Germany make it a distinctive institution within the German higher education landscape.
Rostock itself is a medium-sized city located on the Baltic Sea in the federal state of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern. With a population of about 200,000, it offers a balanced mix of urban life and coastal atmosphere. The city is known for its maritime heritage, historic architecture, and proximity to beaches and nature. Students benefit from a well-developed public transport system, a lively cultural scene, and a strong student presence in the city. Rostock’s location also makes it an ideal starting point for exploring northern Germany and the Baltic region during an exchange semester.

name: University of Stuttgart
description:
The University of Stuttgart is a leading public university in Germany, founded in 1829, with a strong academic tradition and a student population of around 22,000. It is organized into ten faculties and offers a broad spectrum of disciplines in the humanities, social sciences, and cultural studies, alongside its technical and scientific profile. The university is known for its structured approach to teaching and research, and for fostering close collaboration between students and academic staff. Its central location within the city and its integration into regional academic networks make it a well-connected and accessible institution for exchange students.
Stuttgart, the capital of Baden-Württemberg, is a major urban center in southwestern Germany with a population of approximately 630,000. The city combines a rich cultural heritage with a modern infrastructure and a strong focus on education and innovation. Students in Stuttgart benefit from a wide range of cultural institutions, public parks, and recreational opportunities, as well as efficient public transport and proximity to other cities and regions. The surrounding area, including the Swabian Jura and Black Forest, offers excellent possibilities for day trips and outdoor activities. Stuttgart’s dynamic atmosphere and student-friendly environment make it a compelling destination for a semester abroad.

name: University of Tübingen
description:
The University of Tübingen, officially the Eberhard Karl University of Tübingen, is a public
research university located in the city of Tübingen, Baden-Württemberg, Germany. The
University of Tübingen is one of eleven German Excellence Universities.

name: Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology
Aristotle University of Thessaloniki
description:
The Aristotle University of Thessaloniki is the largest university in Greece. The main campus is located in the centre of the city of Thessaloniki, and covers an area of about 33.4 hectares. It comprises 10 faculties which consist of 40 schools and 1 single-School Faculty.
Some educational and administrative facilities are located off campus for practical and operational reasons. A number of these facilities are located outside the city of Thessaloniki or even in other cities.

name: Athens University of Economics and Business
description:
Athens University of Economics and Business (AUEB), founded in 1920, is Greece’s leading institution in the fields of economics, business, and information sciences. With eight academic departments spanning economics, international and European studies, business administration, marketing, accounting, informatics, and statistics, AUEB offers a strong academic foundation rooted in both theory and applied research. The university also hosts a variety of postgraduate programs, many of which are taught in English, and it maintains active participation in European exchange programs like Erasmus+. Known for its international outlook, research excellence, and highly qualified faculty, AUEB provides a rigorous and relevant education, especially for students interested in global business and economic issues.
Located in the heart of Athens, the university gives students easy access to a lively and culturally rich city. From ancient landmarks and bustling markets to cafés and local neighborhoods, Athens blends history and modern energy in a way few European cities can. Exchange students benefit from being part of a dynamic urban environment, with opportunities to explore the city’s vibrant culture while studying in a well-connected central location. The combination of strong academics and an exciting city life makes AUEB an appealing choice for students looking to deepen their knowledge of economics and business while experiencing life in the Greek capital.

name: National and Kapodistrian University of Athens
description: The Faculty of Law offers courses of general legal education and specialization courses at an undergraduate and postgraduate level. The educational process on an interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary level is not confined within the University of Athens, but is realized in cooperation with famous higher education institutions in Greece and abroad. Graduates of The Faculty of Law excel in all fields of science and research; engage in significant professional activity in both Greece and the international scientific world; contribute to the political life and have played a significant role in the construction of the modern Greek state.

name: Panteion University of Social and Political Sciences
description:
Panteion University of Social and Political Sciences, founded in 1927, is one of Greece’s oldest and most respected institutions dedicated exclusively to the social sciences. With around 19,000 students, it offers a wide range of undergraduate and postgraduate programs across departments such as Political Science, Sociology, Psychology, International and European Studies, Communication, Public Administration, and Economic and Regional Development. The university is known for its interdisciplinary academic approach, strong emphasis on research, and its role in shaping social and political thought in Greece.
Situated in the Kallithea district of Athens, Panteion benefits from a central urban location with easy access to cultural landmarks, parks, and the city’s vibrant everyday life. The university is well connected to the rest of Athens via public transport, making it simple to explore both the historical and modern sides of the city. Students often enjoy the nearby neighborhoods filled with local cafés, bookshops, and outdoor spaces, all contributing to a lively and engaging study abroad experience.

name: University of Crete
description:
The University of Crete, established in 1973, is a public, research-oriented institution with campuses in Rethymno and Heraklion. It serves a student body of approximately 20,000 undergraduates and 2,500 postgraduates, supported by over 500 academic staff and 420 administrative personnel. The university is organized into five schools and sixteen departments, offering a wide range of academic disciplines. It is known for its strong emphasis on research and international collaboration, participating actively in European programs such as Erasmus and maintaining partnerships with institutions across Europe and the United States. A unique feature of the University of Crete is its close integration with regional research centers, including the Foundation for Research and Technology – Hellas (FORTH), which enhances opportunities for students to engage in high-level scientific work.
Crete, the largest and most populous of the Greek islands, offers a rich cultural and natural environment for students. The island combines ancient history, Mediterranean landscapes, and a vibrant local culture shaped by diverse influences from Europe, North Africa, and the Middle East. Students can explore archaeological sites, hike through dramatic gorges, and enjoy local cuisine rooted in the renowned Cretan diet. Public transport connects the university campuses with nearby towns and beaches, making it easy to experience the island’s varied offerings. A fun fact: Crete is home to two of the world’s few pink sand beaches, Balos and Elafonissi, adding a unique natural attraction to the student experience.

name: Ilisimatusarfik - University of Greenland
description:
The University of Greenland, known as Ilisimatusarfik, is the leading institution of higher education in Greenland and offers a unique academic experience shaped by Arctic perspectives. It is a small university with around 200 to 300 students. The university offers courses mainly in Greenlandic and Danish, with some courses available in English. The main campus is located in Nuuk.
Nuuk is a small yet dynamic city surrounded by dramatic mountains and fjords, offering a blend of traditional Greenlandic culture and modern living. The city is compact and walkable, with short distances between most areas. The natural surroundings provide endless opportunities for outdoor exploration, including hiking, kayaking, and witnessing the northern lights, making it an inspiring place for students seeking both cultural immersion and adventure.

name: Eötvös Loránd University
description:
Eötvös Loránd University (ELTE), established in 1635, is Hungary's oldest and largest university, renowned for its academic excellence and research contributions. Situated in Budapest, ELTE offers a diverse range of programs across various disciplines, including humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, and law. The university provides courses in English, making it accessible to international students. With a commitment to fostering a dynamic learning environment, ELTE encourages critical thinking, interdisciplinary collaboration, and global perspectives. Students have the opportunity to engage in cutting-edge research and benefit from the expertise of distinguished faculty members.
Located in the heart of Budapest, ELTE's campuses offer a blend of historical charm and modern facilities. The city, known for its rich cultural heritage and vibrant atmosphere, provides students with a unique living and learning experience. Budapest boasts a wide array of cultural attractions, including museums, theaters, and historic landmarks, as well as a lively student community. The city's efficient public transportation system ensures easy access to various parts of Budapest, allowing students to explore and immerse themselves in the local culture. Studying at ELTE offers not only academic growth but also the chance to experience life in one of Europe's most captivating cities.

name: Reykjavik University
description:
Reykjavik University is a modern and innovative institution which has around 3,500 students, creating a close and collaborative learning environment. The university offers a wide range of courses taught in English, particularly at the undergraduate and graduate levels. Its main campus is located in central Reykjavik, designed with open spaces and modern facilities that encourage creativity and cooperation among students.
Reykjavik, the capital of Iceland, is a small yet lively city surrounded by breathtaking natural scenery. It is known for being safe, friendly, with well-planned paths and compact neighborhoods that make daily life convenient. The city offers a rich cultural scene with music, art, and festivals throughout the year, as well as cozy cafes and geothermal pools that reflect the local lifestyle. Just outside the city, students can enjoy stunning landscapes such as volcanic fields, waterfalls, and coastal views, making Reykjavik an ideal place to combine academic studies with outdoor adventure.

name: University of Akureyri
description:
Akureyri, a city with significant influence on the development of Northern Iceland, has emerged as a vibrant center of learning. Despite its remote location, trade and export, particularly of seafood products, have facilitated connections with the outside world. With a population of around 17,000, Akureyri is the largest community outside the Reykjavik area. The establishment of the University of Akureyri in 1987 solidified the city's reputation as an educational hub.
The University of Akureyri, home to approximately 2,000 students, boasts two campuses. Alongside academic facilities, the university campus offers a cafeteria, a wellness and exercise center, and a 24/7 accessible library. Embrace the enriching educational opportunities and the lively atmosphere of Akureyri as you embark on your academic journey at the University of Akureyri.
.

name: University of Iceland
description:
The University of Iceland is the country’s oldest and largest university, with roughly 14,000 students enrolled across undergraduate, graduate, and PhD programmes. It comprises five schools and over 25 faculties, offering more than 400 programmes in many fields including sciences, humanities, health and social sciences. Classes are mainly taught in Icelandic, but there is a growing number of English-taught courses, especially at Master’s level.
Reykjavík offers a vibrant cultural life, easy access to nature, and a welcoming atmosphere. You’ll be close to museums, cafés and arts events, while also having quick access to outstanding natural beauty: volcanic landscapes, geothermal pools, glaciers, waterfalls and long summer days (or northern lights in winter).

name: Sri Venkateswara College – University of Delhi
Trinity College Dublin
description:
Trinity College Dublin, founded in 1592 by royal charter, is Ireland’s oldest and most prestigious university and the sole college of the University of Dublin. Located on a 47-acre historic campus in the heart of Dublin, it serves around 22,000 undergraduate and postgraduate students across three faculties: Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences; Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics; and Health Sciences. Trinity is internationally recognized for academic excellence and offers a broad range of programs across disciplines such as business, law, engineering, science, and the arts. The university fosters independent intellectual inquiry, interdisciplinary collaboration, and creativity, and is consistently ranked as Ireland’s leading university and among the top 100 globally in various fields.
Trinity is committed to research excellence and societal impact, with world-class interdisciplinary research centres focused on areas like sustainable development, global health, artificial intelligence, and biodiversity. The university hosts a diverse and international academic community, with students and staff from over 120 countries. Trinity encourages a broad-based education, allowing students to explore subjects outside their primary field of study and develop critical thinking skills. With strong links to global industries and institutions, and a location in Dublin’s innovation and cultural hub, Trinity offers an education that is both academically rigorous and closely connected to real-world opportunities.

name: University College Cork
description:
University College Cork (UCC) is one of Ireland’s leading universities, known for its strong academic reputation and commitment to research and innovation. It serves a diverse student body of over 24,000 and offers a wide range of disciplines across its faculties. UCC places a strong emphasis on sustainability, international collaboration, and student-centered learning. The university integrates research with teaching and encourages students to engage with real-world challenges through interdisciplinary approaches and community partnerships. Its campus combines historic architecture with modern facilities, creating a balanced environment for academic and personal development.
Cork, located in the south of Ireland, is a lively and welcoming city with a rich cultural heritage and a strong student presence. The city is compact and easy to navigate, with good public transport and a wide range of cafés, music venues, and cultural events. Students can explore nearby coastal areas, historic sites, and scenic countryside, all within easy reach. A fun fact: Cork is home to one of the world’s largest natural harbours and also produces a significant share of the world’s Tic Tacs.

name: University College Dublin
description:
University College Dublin, founded in 1854, is Ireland’s largest university and one of Europe’s leading research-intensive institutions. With over 39,000 students, including a vibrant international community, UCD offers a broad academic portfolio across six colleges in disciplines such as business, social sciences, law, science, engineering, medicine, agriculture, and the humanities. The university places strong emphasis on academic excellence, interdisciplinary learning, and real-world application of knowledge. Courses are taught by leading researchers, and exchange students are welcomed into a dynamic and inclusive academic environment. UCD’s modern campus provides state-of-the-art facilities, world-class libraries, and numerous research centres that support an active and engaged learning experience.
Located just south of Dublin city centre, UCD’s Belfield campus combines the convenience of urban living with the calm of a self-contained, green setting. Dublin is a lively and welcoming capital known for its cultural richness, literary history, and friendly atmosphere. Exchange students at UCD benefit not only from a high-quality education but also from easy access to music, theatre, museums, cafés, and nature. The city’s excellent public transport and international connectivity make it a great base for travel and exploration. Living and studying in Dublin offers a well-balanced student experience that blends academic challenge with social and cultural discovery.

name: University of Limerick
description:
The University of Limerick (UL), founded in 1972 and granted university status in 1989, is a forward-thinking, research-led institution known for its strong emphasis on innovation, collaboration, and real-world learning. UL offers a wide range of academic programs through its four faculties: Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences; Education and Health Sciences; Science and Engineering; and the Kemmy Business School, which holds prestigious international accreditations. The university is particularly noted for its co-operative education model, which integrates work placements into many degree programs, and its close partnerships with industry and public institutions. With a student population of around 16,500, including a thriving community of international and exchange students, UL provides a supportive and dynamic academic environment.
Located on a scenic riverside campus just outside the city of Limerick, the university blends modern architecture with natural beauty. The campus is known for its welcoming atmosphere, green spaces, and iconic footbridges across the River Shannon. Limerick itself is a friendly, student-oriented city that offers a rich cultural life, from galleries and music venues to sports and local festivals. Its manageable size, affordability, and lively student scene make it an appealing destination for international students. Whether you're exploring the nearby Wild Atlantic Way or enjoying the strong sense of community on campus, studying at UL offers a well-rounded experience both academically and personally.

name: Hebrew University of Jerusalem
description:
The Hebrew University of Jerusalem, Israel’s first university, is a multidisciplinary institution of higher learning and research where intellectual pioneering, cutting-edge discovery and a passion for learning flourish. It is a center of international repute, with ties extending to and from the worldwide scientific and academic community and where teaching and research interact to create innovative approaches that ensure the broadest of educations for its students.
Ranked among the world’s leading universities, at the Hebrew University Israelis of all backgrounds receive a university education where excellence is emphasized; where advanced, postgraduate study and research are encouraged; and where special programs and conferences attract students and academics from around the world. At its core, the Hebrew University’s mission is to develop cutting-edge research, to educate future leaders in all walks of life, and to nurture future generations of outstanding scientists and scholars in all fields of learning.

name: Ca' Foscari University of Venice
description:
Ca’ Foscari University of Venice, established in 1868 as Italy’s first business school, has evolved into a comprehensive institution offering a wide array of academic programs. With approximately 20,000 students and eight departments, the university is structured around four main academic areas: Foreign Languages and Literatures, Humanities, Economics, and Sciences. Exchange students have access to a diverse selection of courses, including subjects in international business, cultural studies, environmental science, and linguistics, many of which are offered in English. Ca’ Foscari maintains a strong emphasis on global engagement and intercultural exchange, providing international students with academic experiences deeply connected to the university’s historical strengths in commerce, languages, and cultural heritage.
Situated in the heart of Venice, Ca’ Foscari’s campuses are embedded within the city’s iconic canals and historic architecture. The unique urban landscape offers students a learning environment that blends academic life with the artistic, cultural, and maritime traditions of Venice. From exploring local markets and museums to participating in university-organized cultural events, exchange students experience daily life in a city renowned for its beauty, history, and vibrant student atmosphere. The University also offers Italian language courses for international students and a ‘buddy’ program with local students.

name: Luiss (Rome)
description:
Luiss University, officially Libera Università Internazionale degli Studi Sociali Guido Carli, is a renowned private university in Rome specializing in the social sciences. Established in 1974, Luiss offers academic programs across four main departments: Economics and Finance, Business and Management, Law, and Political Science. The university emphasizes a practical and interdisciplinary approach to learning, closely connected with Italy’s business community and public institutions. Exchange students have access to a broad selection of English-taught courses, with opportunities to engage in case studies, project work, and interactive seminars designed to mirror real-world challenges. A favorable student-to-faculty ratio ensures personalized learning and active academic engagement.
Located in Rome’s elegant Parioli and Trieste neighborhoods, Luiss University provides a campus environment within one of Europe’s most historic and dynamic cities. Students can easily explore Rome’s rich cultural life, with museums, galleries, markets, and iconic landmarks just a short distance from campus. The university fosters a vibrant student community through various academic and cultural events, allowing exchange students to immerse themselves in both Italian university life and the unique urban energy of Rome.

name: The Historical Archives of the European Union, Firenze
Università degli Studi di Napoli Federico II
University of Bergamo
description:
The University of Bergamo, founded in 1968, is a public university known for its strong connection to the local territory and close collaboration with businesses and institutions. The university offers a diverse range of academic programs across its seven departments, including Economics, Engineering, Foreign Languages, Humanities, Law, Education, and Human and Social Sciences. Exchange students have the opportunity to attend courses taught in both Italian and English, particularly in areas like business, economics, engineering, and languages. The university promotes an interdisciplinary approach, blending theoretical study with practical experiences through workshops, research projects, and partnerships with local industries.
Bergamo itself is a charming city in northern Italy, located at the foothills of the Alps and just a short distance from Milan. The city’s rich medieval heritage, vibrant cultural scene, and compact size make it an ideal setting for international students seeking an immersive and accessible study abroad experience. Students can enjoy a lively atmosphere with festivals, concerts, and university events, while also having easy access to nature, mountain activities, and major urban hubs in the Lombardy region.

name: University of Bologna
description:
The University of Bologna, founded in 1088, is widely recognized as the oldest university in the Western world and a prestigious center of academic excellence. With over 90,000 students and a strong international profile, the university offers a vast selection of courses across its 32 departments and five campuses. Exchange students can engage in diverse academic fields such as humanities, social sciences, economics, political science, law, engineering, and sciences. The university’s emphasis on interdisciplinary learning, research, and innovation provides students with rich academic experiences deeply rooted in tradition yet oriented towards the future.
Bologna is a vibrant university city, known for its lively student atmosphere, rich cultural heritage, and welcoming environment. The historic city center, with its iconic medieval towers and extensive porticoed streets, offers a dynamic setting where academic life blends seamlessly with local culture, music, art, and cuisine. Its central location in Italy also makes it easy for students to explore other cities and regions, providing an ideal base for cultural and academic exploration.

name: University of Campania Luigi Vanvitelli
description: Situated in Naples, the third largest city in Italy, the University of Campania Luigi Vanvitelli was established in 1991 and today consists of 16 Departments and hosts more than 24,000 students in 5 different locations in and around Naples: Aversa, Caserta, Santa Maria Capua Vetere, Capua, and in Naples.

name: University of Milan
description:
The University of Milan stands as a leading institution in Italy, recognized for its substantial investments in research infrastructure and fostering human capital. With the ever-changing landscape of knowledge, these two elements are crucial in addressing complex societal and industrial challenges. The university comprises eight faculties and two schools, encompassing a wide range of disciplines such as Agricultural and Food Sciences, Exercise and Sports Sciences, Humanities, Law, Linguistic and Cultural Mediation Sciences, Medicine, Pharmacy, Political, Economic & Social Sciences, Science & Technology, and Veterinary Medicine.
In terms of student life, the university offers opportunities for engagement and enrichment beyond the classroom. The University Sports Centre (CUS) serves as an amateur sports association that has been promoting and organizing university sporting activities for over 70 years. Students have access to a variety of sports at affordable rates, both within the center's events and in affiliated sports facilities. Moreover, the university has established a network of relationships and signed agreements with cultural institutions and associations in Milan and other cities. This allows for vibrant cultural exchanges between the academic and local communities, providing students with discounts at museums, theaters, cinemas, and more, further enhancing their educational experience. Through its commitment to research, education, and the holistic development of its students, the University of Milan remains at the forefront of academic excellence and actively contributes to the intellectual, cultural, and social fabric of both Milan and the wider academic community.

name: University of Pavia
description:
The University of Pavia, founded in 1361, is one of the oldest universities in Europe and continues to be a prominent academic institution in Italy. It hosts over 26,000 students and employs more than 1,000 teaching and research staff across 18 departments. The university is known for its strong emphasis on interdisciplinary research and international collaboration, with several research centers and partnerships worldwide. A distinctive feature of the University of Pavia is its network of historic student residences, known as collegi, which offer a unique community experience and foster academic and personal development beyond the classroom.
Located in the Lombardy region of northern Italy, the city of Pavia offers a balanced blend of cultural heritage and student-friendly living. With a population of around 70,000, it is compact and easy to navigate, making it ideal for students seeking a quieter environment while still being close to Milan, one of Europe’s major urban centers. The city is rich in history, with Romanesque churches, medieval towers, and Renaissance architecture scattered throughout its streets. A fun fact: Pavia is home to one of the oldest botanical gardens in Italy, established in 1773, which remains a peaceful retreat for students and visitors alike.

name: University of Pisa
description:
The University of Pisa, established in 1343, is one of Italy’s most prestigious public universities, with a long-standing tradition in scientific and humanistic research. It currently hosts over 50,000 students and employs more than 3,000 academic and administrative staff. The university is particularly renowned for its contributions to mathematics, physics, and engineering, and maintains strong ties with national research institutions such as the National Research Council (CNR). A unique aspect of the University of Pisa is its close integration with cutting-edge research facilities, offering students direct access to advanced laboratories and collaborative projects.
Situated in the Tuscany region, the city of Pisa offers students a vibrant yet manageable environment, with a rich historical backdrop and easy access to both coastal and inland destinations. The city is well-connected by public transport and lies just an hour from Florence, making it an ideal base for exploring central Italy. Pisa’s compact size and student-centered atmosphere make it easy to navigate and settle into daily life. A fun fact: while the Leaning Tower is its most famous landmark, Pisa is also home to one of world's oldest botanical gardens, founded in 1544, which continues to serve as a research and teaching facility for the university.

name: University of Salerno
description:
The University of Salerno, with origins dating back to the medieval Schola Medica Salernitana, was formally re-established in 1944 and has since grown into a modern academic institution with over 35,000 students. Located in the town of Fisciano, the university operates a large, integrated campus that brings together teaching, research, and student life in one location. It is particularly recognized for its investment in digital infrastructure and sustainability, offering students access to advanced facilities and a well-organized academic environment. Unlike many Italian universities, the University of Salerno is structured as a campus university, which fosters a strong sense of community and makes student services easily accessible.
The university is situated in the Campania region, just a short distance from the Amalfi Coast and the city of Salerno. This location offers students a mix of natural beauty, historical sites, and modern urban life. Salerno itself is a lively coastal city with a walkable historic center, a scenic promenade, and regular cultural events. The region is well-connected by public transport, making it easy to explore nearby destinations such as Naples, Pompeii, and Paestum.

name: University of Trento
description:
The University of Trento (
Università degli Studi di Trento
) is located in Trento and nearby Rovereto. It has been able to achieve considerable results in didactics, research, and international relations according to CENSIS and the Italian Ministry of Education. The University of Trento was founded in 1962 as a Higher University Institute for Social Sciences. It then became the first Faculty of Sociology in Italy. UniTrento is widely recognized as a dynamic and innovative research and teaching institution with strong connections to industry and top-class services. National and international classifications consistently rank the University of Trento as one of the top Italian universities. In addition to traditional lectures, there is much emphasis on laboratory work and small seminar groups.
UniTrento is a medium-sized university, where it is easy for students and teachers to interact and there is a continuous exchange of ideas across many different disciplines: in short, the virtuous dynamism of a small university. Furthermore, because of long-term international relations, UniTrento is a vibrant, multi-cultural university which fosters an enriching and stimulating learning environment. The university is located in one of the most gorgeous natural environments in the world, the Dolomites, and it combines strong links to the territory with a steady expansion of international outreach.

name: University of Turin
description:
The University of Turin, founded in 1404, is one of Italy’s largest and most respected public universities, with a student population of over 80,000 and more than 4,000 academic and administrative staff. It offers a broad academic portfolio across 27 departments and maintains a strong reputation in both humanities and sciences. The university is known for its commitment to research excellence and internationalization, with numerous partnerships and exchange agreements worldwide. A notable feature is its integration with local institutions and industries, which provides students with opportunities for practical experience and interdisciplinary collaboration within the city and region.
Turin, located in the Piedmont region of northwestern Italy, is a dynamic city with a rich cultural and industrial heritage. It offers students a mix of historical architecture, contemporary art, and green spaces, all within a well-connected urban setting. The city is known for its cafés, museums, and proximity to the Alps, making it attractive for both academic and leisure activities. Public transport is efficient, and the cost of living is generally lower than in other major Italian cities.

name: Chuo University
description:
Chuo University was founded in July 1885 as Igirisu Horitsu Gakko (English Law School) at
Nishiki-cho in the Kanda district of Tokyo.
Chuo University has four campuses in Tokyo, the capital of Japan. The Tama Campus is
surrounded by the lush greenery of suburban western Tokyo; the Korakuen Campus, Ichigaya
Campus and Ichigaya Tamachi Campus are conveniently located in downtown Tokyo. Chuo
University offers fulfilling education opportunities through coordination across all our four
campuses.

name: Kanazawa University
description:
Kanazawa University is the third oldest university in Japan, founded in 1949, and one of the Hokuriku region's major institutions of higher education. Today, it comprises three colleges, 16 schools, five graduate schools, a university hospital, a cancer research institute and other units.
Kanazawa University is divided into two main campuses: Kakuma and Takaramachi. The university enrollment is about 10,100 students, including 636 international students in 2021.

name: Kobe University
description: Kobe University is a leading Japanese national university located in the city of Kobe. It was established in 1949, but the academic origins of Kobe University trace back to the establishment of Kobe Higher Commercial School in 1902, which was renamed as Kobe University of Commerce, and Kobe University of Economics. Kobe University is one of the oldest and largest national universities in Japan, as well as one of the highest ranking national universities in the country. It comprises 14 graduate schools and 11 undergraduate faculties, and holds about 16,000 students enrolled in undergraduate and graduate programs. The institution welcomes overseas students, which accounted for a total of 1,179 students, as of 1 May 2021.

name: Kumamoto University
description:
Kumamoto is located in the center of Kyushu Island in Japan and is rich in nature. KU was
founded in 1756 and is one of the oldest universities in Japan. Today it consists of seven
faculties, eleven graduate schools and 23 research centers/institutes. The university is home to
around 8,000 undergraduate students and 2,000 graduate students, including 507 international
students from 49 countries.

name: Nagoya University
description:
Established in 1996, NUPACE, the Nagoya University Program for Academic
Exchange, constitutes both a frontrunner and intrinsic element of our continued endeavor to
internationalize.
NUPACE will afford you the opportunity to simultaneously enjoy a quality academic
curriculum, discover Japan and, most importantly, to acquire a fundamentally international
approach to life.

name: Nanzan University
description: Nanzan University offers 8 Faculties and 18 Departments, 6 Graduate Schools and 14 Programs, as well as Center for Japanese Studies. Small-size classes enable students to be active in class and easy to get attention and valuable advice from professors. The Center for Japanese Studies is renowned as a leader in the field of Japanese language education for more than 45 years.

name: Ochanomizu University
description:
Ochanomizu University is located in Tokyo, Japan Ochanomizu University can trace its roots
back to 1875 when it was first founded as Tokyo Women’s Normal School (later to be Tokyo
Women’s Higher Normal School) in Tokyo’s Ochanomizu (now Yushima, Bunkyo-ku) as an
institution specializing in the development of female faculties. The origin of the name
Ochanomizu University comes from the location of Ochanomizu. The university is home to
around 82,000 undergraduate students and 800 graduate students.

name: Okayama University
description:
Founded in 1870, Okayama, known as the “Land of Sunshine”, is relatively safe from natural disasters, and the crime rate is low. Okayama University, one of Japan's leading universities, is situated on an extensive campus and has eleven faculties and Master's and Doctoral courses embracing humanities, social, natural, environmental and life sciences, and pedagogics
13,012 students are enrolled at the university, which includes 760 international students from 46 different countries.

name: Osaka University
description:
Although officially founded in 1931 as Japan's 6th imperial university, you may be interested
to learn that Osaka University's roots reach back to 1838 and Tekijuku, a private "place of
learning" founded by OGATA Koan.
Today, Osaka University has four campuses: Suita, Toyonaka, Minoh, and Nakanoshima.
Furthermore, the university boasts 11 undergraduate schools, 16 graduate schools, and 29
centers and institutes for research. It is clearly one of Japan's outstanding comprehensive
universities.

name: Ritsumeikan University
description:
The history of Ritsumeikan dates back to 1869 when Prince Kinmochi Saionji, an eminent international statesman of modern Japan, founded "Ritsumeikan" as a private academy on the site of the Kyoto Imperial Palace. Today, Ritsumeikan University offers a wide range of courses in advanced studies at its Kinugasa Campus in Kyoto, Biwako‐Kusatsu Campus (BKC) in Shiga and Osaka‐Ibaraki Campus (OIC) in Osaka.
The Study in Kyoto Program (SKP) brings together students from around the world. It offers numerous courses in Japanese language and culture, utilizing the extensive historical and cultural resources of the ancient city of Kyoto. The program also offers courses in English regarding both Japan‐related and business subjects.
Kyoto, the capital of Japan from 794 to 1868, is an ideal place for study, being a city with one of the highest concentrations of academic institutions in Japan. Kyoto is home to some of Japan's most important World Heritage Sites such as the Ryoanji, Ninnaji and Kinkakuji (Golden Pavilion) Temples, which are located right at the doorstep of Ritsumeikan University. It enjoys a harmonious blend of the ancient and the modern, thus giving students the unique opportunity to experience all aspects of Japanese society.
By studying in SKP at Ritsumeikan University, students are able to take advantage of the rich academic and cultural environment of this city, leading to a truly fruitful and memorable study experience in Japan.

name: Ryukoku University
description:
Ryukoku University is located in Kyoto, Japan. Ryukoku University has a long history dating back
to the Gakuryo (a Buddhist seminary) academy that was established in the precinct of Nishi-
Hongwanji Temple in 1639. Therefore, Ryukoku University has the longest history of university
education and research in Japan, spanning over 380 years. The university is home to around
20.000 undergraduate students and 1000 graduate students, including around 500 international
students from 32 countries.

name: Tohoku University
description:
Tohoku University, founded in 1907, is one of Japan’s top national research institutions and has a long-standing reputation for academic excellence and innovation. Exchange students can choose from a wide range of courses taught in English across fields such as materials science, engineering, political science, and the humanities. The university also offers opportunities in business-related subjects through its School of Economics and Management, where students can explore topics like finance, international business, and marketing from both theoretical and applied perspectives. Tohoku is known for its research-first philosophy and interdisciplinary approach, and students benefit from small class sizes and close interaction with faculty.
Located in Sendai, a lively city often called Japan’s “City of Trees,” Tohoku University offers an inviting academic environment within a vibrant, student-friendly setting. The city is surrounded by mountains and coastline, making it easy to enjoy nature year-round, while still offering the convenience and culture of a modern urban center. Parks, cafés, art spaces, and festivals help create an engaging atmosphere, and student clubs across academic and cultural interests provide an excellent way for exchange students to connect with peers and get involved in university life.

name: Tokai University
description:
Tokai University is a private university established by Dr. Shigeyoshi Matsumae in1942. "Tokai"
of "Tokai University" refers to the sea to the east of Asia, namely the Pacific Ocean, and
symbolizes the desire to foster a rich spirit and broad perspectives. Tokai University consists of 7
campuses in Sapporo, Takanawa, Yoyogi, Shonan, Isehara, Shimizu and Kumamoto, which are
comprised of 19 schools and colleges made up of 75 departments, majors, and programs. Its
graduate schools offer 17 programs. The total student population is approximately 30,000. The
founding spirit and objectives of Tokai University are to contribute to human society, to foster
active, talented people and to arouse interest in our earth and a sense of responsibility for the
future of mankind. Tokai University's educational guidelines ground these objectives by offering
a sound and reliable way of thinking as a basis for living and cultivating the richness of
humanity. Tokai University maintains academic exchange agreements with more than 120
universities/organizations in approx. 40 countries. A wide range of international exchange
activities are being actively pursued, from those on the academic front involving students,
researchers, joint-research projects, and the exchange of academic resources, to cultural and
athletic exchanges. There are about 960 international students on campus. Tokai University has
five offices abroad: Denmark, Austria, USA (junior college in Hawaii), Korea and Thailand. Tokai
University has since its beginning maintained close ties to Denmark and Danish educational
culture:
Link

name: University of Tokyo
description:
The University of Tokyo, also known as "Todai" was established in 1877 as the first
national university in Japan. As a leading research university, Todai offers courses in
essentially all academic disciplines at both undergraduate and graduate levels and
conducts research across the full spectrum of academic activity. The university aims
to provide its students with a rich and varied academic environment that ensures
opportunities for both intellectual development and the acquisition of professional
knowledge and skills.

name: Waseda University
description:
