Waseda University, established in 1882, has 13 faculties covering 22 research areas. 56,000
students in total and 4,000 foreign students are learning together on campus. The Center for
Japanese Language is an educational institution that provides year round Japanese courses
for Waseda's 1,700 international students.

name: KIMEP University
description: KIMEP University is the oldest and the largest North American-style University in Central Asia. It was founded in 1992 by the decree of Nursultan Nazarbayev, the First President of the Republic of Kazakhstan. KIMEP is an independent not-for-profit educational institution serving a multicultural and multinational student body. It is situated in a modern campus in the center of Almaty, the largest city in Kazakhstan.

name: Maqsut Narikbayev University
description:
MAQSUT NARIKBAYEV UNIVERSITY is located in the capital of Kazakhstan – Astana.
It is a private university with a large campus in the heart of Astana.

name: Ewha Womans University
description:
The name Ewha was bestowed by Emperor Gojong in 1887 to commemorate the beginning
of women’s education in Korea. It serves not merely as a name of this time-honored
institution but as a symbol of the tradition and spirit of women’s education in Korea.
Ewha produces strong students capable of working in all corners of the world through
diverse and practical international exchange programs.
Undergraduate colleges:
College of Liberal Arts , College of Social Sciences, College of Natural Sciences, ELTEC College
of Engineering, College of Music, College of Art & Design, College of Education, College of
Business Administration, College of Science & Industry Convergence, College of Medicine,
College of Nursing, College of Pharmacy, Scranton College , HOKMA College of General
Education
Graduate Schools:
Humanities and Social Sciences, Natural Sciences, Engineering, Arts, Medicine,
Interdisciplinary Program

name: Hankuk University of Foreign Studies
description:
Since its founding in 1954, Hankuk University of Foreign Studies (HUFS) has played a significant
role in reconstructing Korea after the Korean War by producing numerous CEOs and outstanding
diplomats, who are competitive enough to strive forward in the global stage. Now under the
leadership of President InChul Kim, HUFS is currently teaching 45 foreign languages, and stands
as the number one global university in Korea.

name: Jeju National University
description:
Jeju National University (JNU) is the only state-designated Flagship Korean National
University on Jeju, an island that has been awarded UNESCO’s triple crown in the
field of natural science and was dubbed a New Seven Wonders of Nature. Since its
opening in 1952, JNU has worked to cultivate talent who will change the future
under the vision of “the university faithful to the basics and the university prepared
for the future.”
The nation’s university assessment has named JNU as having the best educational
environment in terms of the ratio of full-time professors to students and per capita
educational expenses. This proves that JNU has advanced its educational environment
to the next level. JNU runs 14 colleges, 1 graduate school, 3 professional graduate
schools and 6 specialized graduate schools. Particularly, it boasts of well-established
teacher’s colleges for potential primary and secondary teachers and a comprehensive
medical education system that involves colleges specialized in medicine, pharmacy,
nursing and veterinary medicine.
To nurture global talent, JNU runs a customized curriculum that offers students all
types of courses from fundamental to advanced levels. Currently, JNU has 1,500
international students from nearly 40 countries and networks with an estimated 300
universities from more than 50 countries including the United States. It has fully
established this network of global education and students are encouraged to
participate in its overseas internship program, intensive English education program
and student exchange program.

name: Kangwon National University
description:
Founded as Kangwon Provincial Chuncheon Agricultural College in 1947, KNU extended to
comprehensive university in 1978 Kangwon National University is as a core national university
representing Gangwon-do, nurturing global talents contributing to the advancement of the
nation and region. Kangwon National University is opening its doors wide for foreign students as
well. As one of the 10 core Korean national universities in Korea, we maintain a high level of
quality in education and research, while offering almost all of the various majors desired by the
students a comprehensive university. Our dormitory capacity is among the highest in Korea, and
KNU is located at the beautiful lakeside city Chuncheon, which is only 1 hour away from the
capital city of Seoul, the center of politics, economy, and culture in Korea, meaning that you can
enjoy a wide variety of cultural activities. Furthermore, our safe and clean living environments
and inexpensive living cost will surely help foreign students studying abroad to live in
comfortably.

name: Keimyung University
description:
Keimyung University (계명대학교, Gyemyeong Daehakgyo), abbreviated as KMU or Keimyung (啓明), is a private university located in
Daegu
, the fourth largest city in
South Korea
. The university takes roots from Jejungwon founded in 1899. The higher education started in 1954 with the support of the leaders of the Northern
Presbyterian
Church of the U.S. as a
Christian
university. KMU is composed of three campuses in the city of
Daegu
, South Korea. They are named for their locations within the city; Daemyeong, which is near the downtown area, Seongseo, which is in the western part of the city, and also Dongsan campus which includes Dongsan Medical Center. The university's Seongseo campus is known as one of the most beautiful campuses in South Korea.

name: Korea University
description:
Korea University was born as “Bosung College” in 1905. With a Royal grant from Emperor
Gojong of the Korean Empire, Lee Yong-ik (Chungsukgong, 1854-1907).
Korea University consists of the Anam Campus (in Seoul), Sejong Campus (in Sejong) and
three auxiliary hospitals (Anam Hospital, Guro Hospital and Ansan Hospital).
The total number of students is 37,493, (Undergraduate: 20,254, Graduate: 9,257) and 7,982
on the Sejong Campus (Undergraduate: 7,031, Graduate: 951).
Among the Anam Campus students 5.81% are international students. The total number of
international students in language, exchange and training programs stands at 2,164.

name: Kyungpook National University
description:
Established in 1946, located in Daegu Republic of Korea. Consists of 17 Colleges, 68
Departments(26 Schools) Kyungpook National University ranked No. 99 in the world, No. 3 in
Korea and No. 1 national university in the World University Impact Rankings 2020 announced by
Times Higher Education (THE), a British global university evaluation agency.

name: Seoul National University
description:
The origin of Seoul National University (SNU) dates back to the late nineteenth century when
Korean Emperor Gojong established modern higher education institutions, which later
became part of SNU.
Seoul National University honors the ideals of liberal education and aims to teach students a
lifelong love of learning that will form the basis for continuous personal growth.
SNU consists of:
16 Colleges, 1 Graduate School and 10 Professional Schools
2,632 full-time faculty members
16,496 undergraduate students and 11,490 graduate students

name: Sogang University
description:
Sogang University was founded in 1960 by the Society of Jesus to provide an education based on
Catholic beliefs and inspired by the Jesuit philosophy of education, in conformity with the
Korean tradition of education. Today there are 27 departments in 9 schools offered in the
undergraduate program with 8.000 students. There are 12 graduate schools with 4.000 students
enrolled. Approximately 5.000 foreign students study annually at Sogang University.

name: Sungkyunkwan University
description:
The university is highly ranked in Asia and is also the oldest in East Asia. Focuses on both
traditions and innovation. Very interested in global collaboration and outlook and known for its
strong academic profile. The university is divided into two campuses: Humanities and social
sciences in central Seoul, natural sciences in Suwon. The university has 26,000 Bachelor’s degree
students and 8,000 Master’s degree students

name: Sungshin Women's University
description:
Sungshin University was founded in 1936 with the the following educational mottos: Sungshin
(act with sincerity and faith), Jishin (strive for new knowledge and Jadong (be independent).
Today Sungshin University is comprised of 13 undergraduate colleges, 5 graduate schools and
approximately 13.000 students enrolled. Sungshin is a women university but male exchange
students are welcome. Male students are also enrolled at the graduate schools.

name: Yeungnam University
description:
Yeungnam University is a private research university located in
Gyeongsan
,
North Gyeongsang
,
South Korea
. The university's predecessors, Taegu College and Chunggu College, were founded in
Daegu
in 1947 and 1950 respectively. In 1967, the two colleges were merged by President
Park Chung Hee
to form Yeungnam University. In 1972, the university's new main campus opened in
Gyeongsan
east of
Daegu
.

name: Yonsei University
description: Since its establishment in 1885, Yonsei University has been at the forefront of higher education. The "Yonsei Legacy" is a unique and powerful one. It blends tradition with the vision of maintaining its stature as one of the most modern, forward-looking, and liberal universities in Asia. Today, Yonsei is recognized by the global community as one of the most innovative and globalized universities.

name: Latvian Academy of Sport Education
description:
The Latvian Academy of Sport Education (LASE) is located in Riga, the capital of Latvia. LASE is the only education institution of a specialized university type in Latvia that trains sport specialists. LASE offers accredited education programmes and trains certified specialists to work in institutions and organizations in the field of education and sport.
LASE students have opportunities to train and participate in different kinds of competitions, representing the Academy on the Latvian and world level. LASE also offers study possibilities for those who do not want to excel so much in sport, but who prefer to facilitate people’s health as a physical education teacher, a recreation specialist, or a sport manager.

name: Riga Graduate School of Law
description: Riga Graduate School of Law (RGSL) is a specialized law school located in Riga, Latvia. RGSL offers interdisciplinary bachelor and masters programmes in law, allowing engaged and curious students to combine their law studies with courses in business, international relations, finance and diplomacy.

name: University of Latvia
description:
The university is located in Riga, the capital of Latvia.
The main building and the international office is localted centrally. Facultiues and dorms are located 10-20 mins away by foot or public transport.
LU has a buddy programme for inbound exchange students.
LU welcomes exchange students from all over the world.

name: American University of Beirut
description: Founded in 1866, the American University of Beirut is a teaching-centered research university based on the American liberal arts model of higher education. AUB has over 8,000 students and 800 faculty members. The University encourages freedom of thought and expression and seeks to graduate men and women committed to creative and critical thinking, lifelong learning, personal integrity, civic responsibility, and leadership.

name: Lithuanian Sports University
description:
Lithuanian Sports University (LSU), founded in 1934, is a specialised public higher education institution that has developed its unique traditions in sport, leisure and health sciences. LSU is known as a leading academic and research centre in sports science in the Baltic Sea region.
The LSU offers 19 degree study programmes at all three study cycles (8 undergraduate, 9 Master’s and 2 PhD), mainly in sport science, where studies, research and practice are closely interconnected.
3 good reasons why you should choose LSU as your destination for exchange:
1. Sports science traditions since 1934
2. A strong focus on sport, physical activity, rehabilitation, and recreation
3. Kaunas is a city with a youthful atmosphere and a rapidly growing number of international students.

name: Vilnius University
description: Mykolas Romeris University (MRU) was founded in 1990 as a non-profit public university located in the urban setting of the large city of Vilnius. The University’s is highly recognized for its’ outstanding Law School and it is no. 1 in the area of Law among all Lithuania’s universities according to “QS World University Rankings by Subject 2020”. In the students’ opinion, the University MRU is also placed no. 1 among all Lithuania’s universities (“Reitingai” magazine, 2020).

name: National Autonomous University of Mexico
description:
Visit the
main university website
to explore UNAM.

name: Universidad de las Américas Puebla
description:
Please read the
UDLAP Magazine
for additional information abot the city, university, campus etc.

name: Universidad Michoacana de San Nicolás de Hidalgo
Delft University of Technology
description:
Top education and research are at the heart of the oldest and largest technical university in the Netherlands. 8 faculties offer 16 bachelor’s and more than 30 master’s programmes. More than 25,000 students and 6,000 employees share a fascination for science, design, and technology.
The university is located in the historic city of Delft in Netherlands, in the heart of Europe. Delft Technical University offers a good balance between theory and practice, project work and hands-on experience at their outstanding research facilities, which will enable you to gain the skills covering future needs.
TU Delft is a highly valued and rated institution recognized worldwide for the quality of its academic environment. Exchange students at TU Delft enrich the academic culture and offer an invaluable contribution to learning.

name: Erasmus University Rotterdam
description:
Erasmus University Rotterdam is a leading international research university known for its strong focus on societal impact and academic excellence. Established in 1913, the university offers a wide range of programs in economics, business, law, social sciences, health, and humanities. It is particularly renowned for its Erasmus School of Economics and Rotterdam School of Management, both of which enjoy global recognition. With a student population of over 30,000, including a large international community, Erasmus University fosters an intellectually stimulating and diverse academic environment. Its interdisciplinary approach and emphasis on real-world relevance make it an ideal destination for students seeking a forward-thinking and globally connected exchange experience.
Located in the vibrant city of Rotterdam, the university offers students the opportunity to live and study in one of Europe’s most innovative urban centers. Rotterdam is known for its modern architecture, dynamic cultural scene, and status as a major international port city. The city’s youthful energy, excellent public transport, and wide range of cultural and recreational activities make it especially appealing to students. Whether exploring contemporary art museums, attending music festivals, or enjoying the city’s waterfront, exchange students will find Rotterdam to be a lively and inspiring place to complement their academic journey at Erasmus University.

name: Hanze University of Applied Sciences
description:
Hanze University of Applied Sciences, located in Groningen, is the largest university of applied sciences in the northern Netherlands. It serves a student population of around 27,000 from over 80 nationalities and offers a wide range of bachelor’s and master’s programmes in fields such as business, engineering, health, arts, and communication. The university emphasizes practical learning through internships, applied research, and close collaboration with industry. Hanze is also home to unique facilities like the Minerva Art Academy and the Prince Claus Conservatoire, making it one of the few institutions in the country to combine technical, business, and artistic education under one roof.
Groningen is a vibrant student city where one in four residents is enrolled in higher education. Known for its youthful energy, the city offers a lively cultural scene, extensive cycling infrastructure, and a strong sense of community. Students enjoy affordable living, safe streets, and a wide range of activities—from music festivals and art exhibitions to outdoor adventures in nearby parks and lakes. A fun fact: Groningen hosts the largest pub in Europe,
De Drie Gezusters
, with over 3,700 seats and 20 bars under one roof—making it a popular spot for students to unwind and socialize.

name: Leiden University
description:
Leiden University, founded in 1575, is the oldest university in the Netherlands and one of Europe’s leading research institutions. It serves nearly 34,000 students from over 120 nationalities and employs more than 6,400 staff members. The university is spread across two cities—Leiden and The Hague—and is home to 32 research institutes that focus on interdisciplinary collaboration across fields such as law, life sciences, artificial intelligence, and global governance. With a strong emphasis on academic freedom and integrity, Leiden University integrates research and teaching, encouraging students to engage with complex societal challenges in a global context.
The city of Leiden offers a rich and student-friendly environment, combining historical charm with modern amenities. Known for its picturesque canals, vibrant cultural scene, and compact layout, Leiden is easy to navigate—most places are just a short bike ride away. The city hosts numerous festivals, museums, and events throughout the year, and is well-connected to other Dutch cities like Amsterdam and The Hague. A fun fact: Leiden is the birthplace of Rembrandt van Rijn and also home to the world’s oldest university observatory, established in 1633—making it a city where art and science have long flourished side by side.

name: Maastricht University
description: Maastricht University was founded in 1976, making it the second youngest of the thirteen Dutch universities. Maastricht University, the European university of the Netherlands, has nearly 22,000 students and 5,000 staff. We are young, interdisciplinary and socially engaged, which is evident in everything we do. Despite our relatively recent establishment, we have already built a strong reputation through our excellent research and education, and by connecting science with regional, European and global challenges. We rank among the best young universities in the world.

name: TILBURG UNIVERSITY
description:
Tilburg University was founded in 1927. The university has a student body of 30,000 students, making 1 in 8 of the people of Tilburg a student. Tilburg University consists of five different schools: Economics & Management, Law, Social and Behavioral Sciences, Humanities and Digital Sciences, and Theology.
According to the three most renowned university rankings (THE, ARWU and QS), Tilburg University belongs to the best 2% of the world’s 17,000 universities!

name: University of Amsterdam
description:
The University of Amsterdam (UvA) is one of Europe’s top research universities, known for its academic excellence, broad disciplinary offerings, and strong international orientation. Founded in 1632, UvA offers a wide range of programs across seven faculties, including humanities, social and behavioral sciences, economics and business, law, and science. With over 40,000 students, including a large international cohort, the university fosters a vibrant and diverse academic community. UvA is particularly recognized for its research-led teaching, interdisciplinary collaboration, and commitment to addressing global challenges through innovative scholarship.
Located in the heart of Amsterdam, the university offers students the opportunity to study in one of the most culturally rich and globally connected cities in Europe. Amsterdam is known for its historic canals, world-class museums, and dynamic urban life. The city’s compact layout, excellent public transport, and welcoming atmosphere make it ideal for student living. Whether exploring the city’s artistic heritage, engaging in public debates, or enjoying its lively cafés and green spaces, exchange students at UvA will find themselves in an inspiring environment that supports both academic growth and personal discovery.

name: University of Groningen
description:
The University of Groningen is one of the oldest and most respected universities in the Netherlands, offering a broad academic portfolio across eleven faculties. It serves a diverse student population of over 30,000 and is known for its strong emphasis on research, innovation, and international collaboration. The university integrates academic learning with practical experience and encourages students to engage with global challenges through interdisciplinary approaches. Its campus combines historic buildings with modern facilities, and students benefit from a wide range of extracurricular activities and support services.
Groningen is a lively and youthful city, often referred to as the student capital of the north. With nearly a quarter of its population enrolled in higher education, the city offers a vibrant atmosphere and a strong sense of community. It is known for its bike-friendly infrastructure, cultural events, and accessible public transport. Students can enjoy museums, music festivals, and green spaces, all within a compact and walkable city center. A fun fact: Groningen is home to the largest pub in Europe,
De Drie Gezusters
, which features over 3,700 seats and 20 bars under one roof.

name: Utrecht University
description: Utrecht University is one of Europe's leading research universities, recognised internationally for its high-quality, innovative approach to research and teaching. Studying at Utrecht University means studying at one of the world's best universities.

name: Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam
description:
The Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam (VU or VU Amsterdam) is a public research university in Amsterdam, Netherlands, founded in 1880. The VU is one of two large, publicly funded research universities in the city, the other being the University of Amsterdam (UvA). The translation of the Dutch name Vrije Universiteit is "Free University". "Free" refers to independence of the university from both the State and the Dutch Reformed Church. Both within and outside the university, the institution is commonly referred to as "the VU".
VU Amsterdam is a unique university with faculties in the humanities, STEM, social sciences and medical sciences. Our education and research are closely linked. We combine our top position in research with a strong social orientation, which has resulted in an excellent international reputation. Our education and research are distinctly multidisciplinary. This is reinforced by the fact that our faculties are all located on one campus. We are a true campus university in the heart of the Zuidas Knowledge District, sharing its excellent national and international position and accessibility. The VU has more than 29.500 students.

name: Wageningen University
description:
In Wageningen, you learn about nature, sustainability and improving everyone's life daily. "To explore the potential of nature to improve the quality of life." That is the mission of Wageningen University & Research (WUR). The strength of WUR lies in its ability to join the forces of specialised research institutes and the university. It also lies in the combined efforts of the various fields of natural and social sciences. This union of expertise leads to scientific breakthroughs that can quickly be put into practice and be incorporated into education. As such, studying in Wageningen guarantees premium quality education and an international quality benchmark on your curriculum vitae.
WUR hosts an international student environment (25 % of the student population) and is less than an hour by train from Amsterdam, making it an ideal destination for exchange students.
WUR consistently ranks as one of the best universities in Europe and the world within Agriculture, Forestry, and Environmental Sciences.

name: Lincoln University
description:
Date of establishment: Established in 1878, Lincoln University is New Zealand’s specialist land-based university, and is ranked in the top 100 universities internationally for agriculture and forestry and the top 500 universities worldwide overall (QS Rankings).
Campus: Location & transportation: Lincoln University is located less than 30 minutes’ drive from Christchurch. Christchurch is becoming one of the world’s leading sustainable cities.With a bustling city centre and a vibrant night life, it’s an ideal environment for students to call home.
Student number: 5,819 students

name: University of Auckland
description:
Founded in 1883, Auckland is the country’s largest university with over 40,000 students, nearly 10,000 of whom graduate annually. The main campus is in the heart of Auckland city and we have four specialist campuses.
The University of Auckland is New Zealand’s world-ranked university. The University of Auckland is the only New Zealand university ranked in the top 200 in the Times Higher Education World University Rankings, in the top 100 in the QS World University Rankings, and with the maximum rating of Five Stars Plus in the QS Stars University Ratings. The University is also the highest ranked New Zealand university in the Shanghai Jiao Tong Academic Ranking of World Universities.
Auckland’s harbour setting, magnificent beaches and verdant bush make it a great place to study and work, while the University’s close proximity to New Zealand’s major business city enables staff and students to rub shoulders with leading practitioners in their field. For example, medical students work alongside leading specialists at Auckland City Hospital while the Faculty of Law is within walking distance of the courts and major legal firms. The Business School has a close relationship with leading Auckland companies and academics from our Faculty of Engineering, School of Population Health and School of Architecture and Planning serve on think-tanks helping to shape the city’s future.
Discover more about living in Auckland

name: University of Canterbury Christchurch
description:
Established in 1873 by scholars from Oxford and Cambridge, the University of Canterbury, in Christchurch, New Zealand, has an international reputation for academic excellence in both teaching and research. Teaching staff are actively involved in research and publishing in their areas of speciality. As a result, even undergraduate students can expect to be taught by lecturers who are at the forefront of knowledge in their field. The University’s world‐class education is also enhanced by the many outstanding international academics who visit each year on our staff exchange programmes. Students may be taught by academic staff from the universities of Oxford or Cambridge, among many others.
The University is situated in a spacious landscaped campus in the suburb of Ilam, Christchurch, only 15 minutes from the central city and 10 minutes from the International Airport. The campus is attractively landscaped, with plenty of green space to relax with friends between lectures. Modern facilities include four libraries, computer suites with 24‐ hour access, lecture theatres, laboratories, studios, six halls of residence and a host of student services and facilities, including cafés, bars, a health centre and pharmacy, recreation facilities, childcare facilities, shops, an art gallery and an events centre.
Learn more about Christchurch

name: University of Otago
description:
Nau mai, haere mai ki Ōtākou Whakaihu Waka – a globally recognised university nestled among the natural beauty of New Zealand’s spectacular South Island. The University of Otago is Aotearoa New Zealand’s first university, founded in 1869, and is the top university in the country for educational performance (TEC Educational Performance Indicators). Our Dunedin campus is recognised as one of the world’s most-beautiful campuses, with impressive historic and modern architecture, situated just a short walk from the main city centre.
Dunedin is Australasia’s only true student city, offering an unmatched student experience with over 20,000 students living, working, and studying in Dunedin, creating an energy and atmosphere you will only find at Otago. Experience a true “kiwi” student lifestyle in the lively neighbourhoods surrounding campus, living as a community in Uniflats, self-catering flats. Otago is ranked #1 in the country for international student learning, with high student satisfaction rates, and world-class research-led teaching. For the adventure seeking student, experience the duality of study and travel that is highly appealing and accessible in Otago. Join our community of international students from more than 100 countries!
Discover the University of Otago through the eyes of our international students!

name: Victoria University of Wellington
description:
Victoria’s teaching and research is built on a proud tradition of academic excellence stretching over more than 100 years. This excellence naturally transfers to, and enriches, the teaching and learning we offer, and illustrates the calibre of discovery and the cutting-edge knowledge of our staff. We are also ranked within the world’s top 150 universities in a significant number of subjects, including law, arts and social sciences, psychology, earth sciences and information technology.
At Victoria, you will join a warm, open and diverse community of students from over 100 countries. Excellent support networks, such as our International Buddy Programme, combined with initiatives like our unique
Kitea Impact Programme
, produce globally aware graduates who are ready for a rapidly changing world. We look forward to welcoming you to Victoria and to Wellington and assisting you to take advantage of the world-class opportunities that are available to you here.
Wellington regularly ranks as one of the most liveable cities in the world. It is compact, safe, friendly, and a great place to live. But don’t take our word for it—come and see for yourself!
Get a glimpe of Wellington has to offer, and why so many people choose to study here.

name: Inland Norway University of Applied Sciences
description:
Inland Norway University of Applied Science is a merger between Lillehammer University college and Hedmark University of Applied Sciences and was deemed effective in 2017.
INN University operates on six campuses in south-eastern Norway: Blæstad, Elverum, Evenstad, Hamar, Lillehammer and Rena and has approximately 13 000 students and 952 employees.

name: Nord University
description:
Global challenges demand new insight, innovative solutions and local legitimacy. Nord University is a young university with strong regional ties and a global perspective.
The faculty has 3350 students at four study locations: Vesterålen, Bodø, Nesna and Levanger.

name: Norwegian School of Theology, Religion and Society
Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)
description:
The Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU) is Norway’s largest university, with about 43,500 students in total, including a significant number of international students. It has campuses in three cities: Trondheim (its main site), Gjøvik, and Ålesund. NTNU offers a wide variety of programmes across many disciplines: science, technology, engineering, health sciences, humanities, social sciences, etc. Many master’s programmes are taught entirely in English, making it quite accessible for exchange students who don’t want to speak Norwegian.
The location and surroundings of NTNU are a major part of its appeal. Trondheim, where the main campus is located, is a lively student city with a strong blend of history, culture, and nature. You get to enjoy river-side areas, a scenic fjord, forests nearby, islands, and plenty of opportunities for outdoor activities like hiking, skiing, or kayaking. The campuses themselves are fairly well integrated into the city, and public transport is good.

name: UiT The Arctic University of Norway
description:
UiT is a large, multi-campus university in Northern Norway, with around 17,000 students, globally recognised as a leading centre for Arctic research. It offers a broad spectrum of programmes across its eight faculties covering most disciplines. While Norwegian is the main language of instruction, many courses especially at the master’s level are taught in English.
The city of Tromsø is often described as really special: you’re surrounded by dramatic Arctic scenery, with fjords, mountains, and islands all nearby, and you get phenomena like the Midnight Sun in summer and Northern Lights in winter. Tromsø is reasonably walkable, especially in the city centre with decent public transit. Importantly, the setting encourages a lot of outdoor activity, both in winter and summer, so if you enjoy nature, you’ll have plenty of options for hiking, skiing, boating, and exploring both urban and wild landscapes.

name: University of Agder
description:
The University of Agder is a modern, dynamic university in southern Norway with about 14,000 students, spread mainly over two campuses in Kristiansand and Grimstad. While many of the undergraduate courses are taught in Norwegian, there is a solid selection of Master’s‐level and exchange courses in English. The Grimstad campus is especially noted for its engineering, technology, and applied sciences orientation, with modern facilities, while Kristiansand is larger, more central, and offers greater diversity in programme choice.
The cities where UiA is based Kristiansand and Grimstad combine the charms of Southern Norway’s coastal landscape with good student amenities and fairly easy living. Kristiansand is the larger city, with a compact centre, decent public transit, green areas, and recreational options close by: forests, beaches, hiking, and water sports. Many services, cafés, shops, and cultural venues are within walking distance if you live in or near the city centre or close to campus, which makes day-to-day life convenient. Grimstad is smaller and the distance from campus to town is short.

name: University of Bergen
description:
The University of Bergen is a public research university located on Norway’s west coast. Established in 1946, it is one of the country’s leading academic institutions, serving around 20,000 students across six faculties. The university offers a wide range of study programmes and is known for its strong focus on interdisciplinary research, particularly in marine sciences, climate studies, and global health.
Bergen, Norway’s second-largest city, offers a unique setting for student life, surrounded by mountains and fjords, making it an ideal place for students who enjoy outdoor activities alongside their studies. The city is compact and walkable, with reliable public transport. Bergen is also known for its rich cultural heritage, vibrant music scene, and historic waterfront district, Bryggen, which is a UNESCO World Heritage site.

name: University of Oslo
description:
The University of Oslo is Norway’s oldest and largest university, founded in 1811, and today home to around 27,000 students. There are more than 800 courses taught in English across all faculties, making it quite accessible for exchange students. The university is spread across several campuses: the major one is Blindern, but there are additional facilities at places like Ullevål and Tøyen.
Oslo, the capital of Norway, offers a unique combination of urban life and natural beauty, making it an attractive destination for students. The city is surrounded by forests and fjords, with outdoor activities like hiking, skiing, and kayaking easily accessible via public transport. Oslo is known for its cultural diversity, vibrant arts scene, and commitment to sustainability. Students can enjoy museums, music festivals, and a lively café culture, all within a compact and walkable city center.

name: University of South-Eastern Norway (USN)
description:
University of South-Eastern Norway is a well-rounded university that serves around 18,000 students, spread across eight campuses. USN was founded following the merger of a number of former university colleges, on January 1st 2016. It offers a wide array of programmes and has courses in both English And Norwegian.
The locations of USN’s campuses provide a unique blend of student life, accessibility and natural surroundings. The surrounding region features scenic landscapes, forests, lakes and smaller towns. Many of the towns where USN is based are compact and quite walkable. Public transit is generally reliable and gives access to Oslo and other hubs.

name: University of Stavanger
description:
The University of Stavanger is a mid-size public research university with around 13,000 students. It offers a wide range of programmes through its six main faculties covering most disciplines. While Norwegian is the main language of instruction, many courses especially at the master’s level are taught in English.
Stavanger is a lively, coastal city in southwest Norway, combining urban amenities with nearby natural beauty. The Ullandhaug campus is about a 12-minute bus ride from the city centre, making it fairly accessible, and there are also good cycling options and public buses that connect campuses and residential areas. In your free time you can explore fjords, beaches, hiking paths, forests nearby, and enjoy cafés, shops and cultural events in Stavanger itself.

name: Western Norway University of Applied Sciences (HVL)
description:
The Western Norway University of Applied Sciences (Høgskulen på Vestlandet - HVL) consists of approximately 17,000 students and 1,400 staff.
It is located on five different campuses: Bergen, Førde, Haugesund, Sogndal and Stord.
From January 1 2017, Bergen University College, Sogn og Fjordane University College and Stord/Haugesund University College have merged to form Western Norway University of Applied Sciences.

name: Al-Quds University
description: Al-Quds University (AQU) is a collegiate research university that currently offers more than 120 undergraduate and postgraduate programs, taught through its fifteen degree-granting faculties that cover the main scientific disciplines such as medicine, life, and natural sciences, business and management, arts and humanities, law and jurisprudence, engineering, and social sciences. Established in 1977, AQU remains the only Arab Palestinian university in Jerusalem, Palestine. AQU currently enrolls around 12,000 full time students, taught by more than 700 faculty members.

name: Pontificia Universidad Católica del Perú
description:

to explore PUCP.

name: Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń
description:
The Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń (NCU) was founded in 1945. It is one of the largest universities in Poland, currently comprising 16 faculties. It provides graduate and postgraduate courses for almost 21,500 students, employing more than 400 staff and offering education in over 100 fields of study and 55 postgraduate courses.
NCU has state-of-the-art research infrastructure including the National Laboratory of Atomic, Molecular and Optical Physics (FAMO), the Center for Quantum Optics and the Interdisciplinary Center for Modern Technologies to name but a few, as well as modern teaching facilities comprising, among others, Collegium Humanisticum and the brand-new University Sports Centre. The Centre for Astronomy in Piwnice near Toruń houses a unique 32-meter radio telescope. Spitsbergen (in the Arctic Sea) is home to NCU Polar Station.

name: University of Warsaw
description:
The University of Warsaw, founded in 1816, holds the distinction of being Poland's largest and most prestigious academic institution. It stands as a beacon of intellectual excellence and research innovation, contributing significantly to the country's scholarly landscape. Located in the vibrant capital city of Warsaw, the university benefits from its dynamic environment, which serves as a center of political, economic, and cultural activity. Warsaw's thriving social scene and rich cultural offerings make it an attractive destination for students seeking a comprehensive educational experience.
Comprising 21 faculties and an impressive 126 buildings, the University of Warsaw covers an extensive range of academic disciplines, including applied linguistics, social sciences, economics, humanities, and natural sciences. With a student population of approximately 40,000, the university fosters an environment that encourages intellectual curiosity, critical thinking, and academic excellence. Yearly appraisals conducted by the university affirm the quality of education, as a majority of students express satisfaction with their choice of institution and academic programs. The University of Warsaw continues to uphold its commitment to delivering world-class education and nurturing the intellectual growth and success of its students.

name: Warsaw University of Life Sciences
description:
Warsaw University of Life Sciences (WULS) – has a nearly 200-year tradition and is one of the oldest and largest universities in Poland.
The university is located in the southern part of Warsaw, approximately 15 km from the city centre. Over 1,300 university teachers and instructors make sure that you will gain plenty of knowledge and practical skills. At present, the university consists of 13 faculties with around 27,000 students enrolled.

name: Egaz og Moniz School of Health and Science
Iscte - University Institute of Lisbon
description:
ISCTE – Instituto Universitário de Lisboa, founded in 1972, is a dynamic public research university located in Lisbon’s university district, currently serving around 11,000 students across four schools: Business, Social and Human Sciences, Sociology and Public Policy, and Technology and Architecture. It offers a wide array of bachelor’s, master’s, integrated master's, and PhD programs in fields such as economics, management, sociology, political science, engineering, and architecture. ISCTE is internationally accredited by organizations like AACSB, AMBA, and EUR-ACE, and hosts strong research centers such as BRU-IUL and DINÂMIA’CET-IUL. With robust global partnerships and a multicultural learning environment, it is an attractive choice for students interested in social sciences, business, technology, and interdisciplinary research.
Living in Lisbon as an ISCTE student combines the energy of a vibrant capital with the charm of student-centered neighborhoods. The ISCTE Students’ Union organizes sports, cultural events, debates, and a range of academic activities that contribute to a lively campus atmosphere. Students also enjoy Lisbon’s bustling cafés, music festivals, rich cultural scene, and easy access to stunning beaches. Altogether, ISCTE offers a rewarding academic experience set in the warm and dynamic environment of Lisbon.

name: Universidade Católica Portuguesa
description:
The Universidade Católica Portuguesa (UCP), established in 1967, is a prominent private university in Portugal with a strong academic and research profile. It operates across four campuses—Lisbon, Porto, Braga, and Viseu—and hosts over 20,000 students, including more than 3,800 international students from 110 nationalities. UCP employs over 1,100 faculty members and maintains 15 research units with nearly 1,500 researchers. The university is known for its interdisciplinary research, international partnerships, and commitment to social responsibility. A distinctive feature of UCP is its status as a concordat university, meaning it operates under a special agreement with the Vatican, which sets it apart from most other institutions in Portugal.
Lisbon, where UCP’s headquarters are located, offers a rich cultural and historical setting for students. The city combines centuries-old architecture with a vibrant modern lifestyle, and is well-connected by public transport, including its iconic yellow trams. Students can enjoy a wide range of cultural activities, from museums and music festivals to traditional Portuguese cuisine. A fun fact: Lisbon’s classic trams are actually based on American streetcars from the early 20th century and were once referred to locally as “Americanos”. This blend of global influences and local traditions makes Lisbon a compelling destination for students seeking both academic and cultural enrichment.

name: UNIVERSITY OF LISBOA
description:
The Universidade de Lisboa (ULisboa), established in its current form in 2013 through the merger of two major institutions, is the largest university in Portugal. It hosts over 50,000 students and comprises 18 schools covering a wide range of disciplines. ULisboa is recognized for its commitment to interdisciplinary research and innovation, with strong international collaborations and a focus on addressing global challenges. Its research agenda is closely aligned with the UN Sustainable Development Goals, and the university actively promotes knowledge transfer and societal impact through partnerships with public and private sectors.
Located in the heart of Lisbon, ULisboa offers students access to a city rich in history, culture, and modern amenities. Lisbon is one of Europe’s oldest continuously inhabited cities, with a legacy that includes Roman galleries, Moorish architecture, and earthquake-resistant urban planning dating back to the 18th century. The city is known for its iconic yellow trams, vibrant neighborhoods, and a growing reputation as a hub for startups and digital innovation. A fun fact: Lisbon’s classic trams are modeled after American streetcars from Harlem and New Orleans, and were once locally referred to as “Americanos”. This blend of tradition and modernity makes Lisbon a compelling destination for students seeking both academic and cultural enrichment.

name: Universidade NOVA de Lisboa
description:
Universidade NOVA de Lisboa, founded in 1973, is a dynamic public university recognized for its innovative spirit and strong international profile. NOVA has grown into one of Portugal’s leading institutions, with around 20,000 students enrolled across nine academic units that cover disciplines ranging from social sciences, humanities, law, and business to science, technology, medicine, and public health. Its schools and faculties consistently rank among the best in Portugal and Europe, known for combining high-quality teaching with research that addresses contemporary challenges. NOVA’s commitment to creating and sharing scientific, cultural, and artistic knowledge, along with training that is deeply anchored in research, reflects its mission to contribute actively to the social and economic development of the communities it serves.
Studying in Lisbon offers students the chance to live in a vibrant European capital known for its mild climate, historical neighborhoods, and rich cultural life. NOVA’s various campuses are well integrated into the city, providing modern facilities and fostering an environment that encourages collaboration, creativity, and global perspectives. With Lisbon’s welcoming atmosphere and excellent quality of life, students at NOVA enjoy both rigorous academic experiences and the benefits of living in a lively, cosmopolitan setting.

name: University of Coimbra
description:
The University of Coimbra, founded in 1290 by King Dinis, is the oldest continuously operating university in Portugal and one of the oldest in the world. Relocated permanently to Coimbra in 1537, it occupies the historic Royal Palace, now known as the Paço das Escolas, and has been recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2013. The university enrolls over 25,000 students, with around 20 percent coming from abroad, and is organized into eight faculties offering a wide range of bachelor’s, master’s, and doctoral programs. Blending centuries of tradition with modern academic excellence, it is especially renowned in fields such as medicine, engineering, social sciences, and the humanities. The campus is home to remarkable landmarks like the Baroque Biblioteca Joanina, which houses tens of thousands of historic volumes, and a botanical garden dating back to 1772.
Living in Coimbra as a student means becoming part of a lively city where academic life and local culture are closely intertwined. The medieval old town and university buildings create a unique atmosphere, deeply shaped by traditions like the student capes and annual ceremonies such as Queima das Fitas and Latada. Students find community through the Associação Académica de Coimbra, the oldest student union in Portugal, which organizes a wide variety of cultural and sports activities, from theater and music to rugby, chess, and rowing. With its scenic riverside location along the Mondego, rich academic heritage, and vibrant student life, Coimbra offers an immersive and memorable university experience.

name: University of Porto
description:
The University of Porto, established in 1911, is one of Portugal’s top public research universities and the country’s second largest by enrollment. It serves around 28,000 students, including approximately 11,000 postgraduate students, across 13 faculties, a business school, and a range of specialized institutes, supported by more than 2,300 academic staff. The university offers a wide selection of programs in fields such as economics, management, engineering, law, humanities, science, and the arts, with over 60 bachelor’s degrees, and more than 160 master’s programs. U.Porto’s mission is to create scientific, cultural, and artistic knowledge, to offer advanced education strongly anchored in research, to drive the social and economic value of knowledge, and to actively contribute to the progress of the communities it serves. Its School of Economics and Management is particularly well regarded, fostering close connections with businesses and international institutions and preparing graduates for competitive global careers.
Living in Porto as a student means enjoying a vibrant, welcoming city known for its rich culture, historic charm, and affordable lifestyle. The cost of living is relatively low compared to many other Western European cities, with budget-friendly options for food, housing, and public transportation. Porto’s extensive metro, bus, and train networks make it easy to explore, while the atmospheric old town, riverside cafés, music venues, and art spaces add to the lively student experience. University associations organize a wide variety of cultural, sports, and volunteer activities that help students quickly feel part of the community. With friendly locals and easy access to Portugal’s coastline and beautiful northern landscapes, studying in Porto offers a dynamic and fulfilling university life.

name: National Research University Higher School of Economics - Moscow
National Research University Higher School of Economics - Nizhny Novgorod
National Research University Higher School of Economics - St. Petersburg
Saint Petersburg University
description:
Founded in 1724, St. Petersburg State University is the oldest institution of higher education in Russia. During the 290 years of its existence University secured the right to be acknowledged as one of the best institutions of higher education in Russia: its rich history, modern large-scale research activities, development and innovations make SPSU ahead of the curve in the field of Russian science.
At present, there are more than 32,000 students in SPSU, receiving education in more than 323 specialties in 24 faculties. SPSU staff comprises almost 14,000 people, including nearly 6,000 teachers (1,000 Doctors of Science, over 2,000 Candidates of Science, 42 Academicians of state academies) who represent 289 academic departments.
SPSU has everything to enjoy studies, hobbies and research: the richest Research Library named after Maksim Gorky, research institutes, museums, the big University publishing house, the University choir of students, graduates and teachers, clubs (from rugby and orienteering to the Ingria search party), etc

name: Universite Cheikh Anta Diop De Dakar
University of Belgrade
description:
The University of Belgrade is Serbia’s largest and oldest university, established in
its first form in 1808. It achieved university status in 1905. The University of
Belgrade has served as a role model for many small universities in Serbia,
Montenegro, Bosnia-Herzegovina and Macedonia.

name: National University of Singapore
description:
NUS started out as a modest medical school in 1905, founded by a determined group of
businessmen led by Tan Jiak Kim, to serve the needs of the local community. Today, we are
Singapore’s flagship university consistently ranked among the top two universities in Asia and
top 25 in the world.
NUS consists of 3 Campuses:
Kent Ridge, Bukit Timah and Outram.
12 Undergraduate Schools, 4 Graduate Schools, 26 University‐level Research Institutes and
Centres.
52 Bachelor's degrees, 28 Double majors, 27 Concurrent degrees, 35 Joint degrees,
71 Double degrees.144 Master's degrees, Doctoral degrees, Graduate diplomas
28000 Undergraduates, 10000 Graduate students, 2400 Faculty and 3200 Research Staff.

name: Singapore Management University
description:
SMU was established on 29 July 2000 and is located in the Downtown area of Singapore. It has a city campus with a total enrolment of about 10,000 undergraduate and postgraduate students and comprises six schools offering undergraduate, graduate and PhD programmes in business administration, business analytics, financial services, accountancy, economics, information systems management, law and the social sciences. The university has over 30 research institutes and centres of excellence, and customised corporate training and lifelong learning for individuals are available through the university's professional and executive development programmes.
SMU comprises six schools:
- School of Accountancy
- Lee Kong Chian School of Business
- School of Economics
- School of Information Systems
- School of Law
- School of Social Sciences
SMU has an emphasis on generating rigorous, high‐impact, and relevant multi‐disciplinary research that addresses Asian issues of global relevance, SMU faculty collaborate with leading international researchers and universities from USA, Europe, China and India as well as with partners in the business community and public sector, through its research institutes, centres and labs.
SMU’s city campus is a state‐of‐the‐art facility located in the heart of downtown Singapore, fostering strategic linkages with business, government and the wider community.

name: Yale-NUS College
description:
Yale-NUS college is a newer college situated on National University of Singapore
campus.
Yale-NUS College is a residential college located at NUS, which aims to redefine
liberal arts and science education for a complex, interconnected world.
We are a diverse group of students, faculty, staff, and supporters, dedicated to
building a community in which living and learning are intertwined and habits of
creativity, curiosity, and critical thinking are encouraged. Our innovative curriculum
integrates knowledge from across the disciplines and around the world.
An intimate liberal arts college, dedicated to undergraduate education, Yale-NUS
draws on the resources and traditions of two great universities. We pursue
excellence through innovative teaching and research, and we provide global
opportunities for our students.
Our location at the crossroads of Asia informs our pedagogy. Drawing on active
modes of learning associated with American liberal arts education, we introduce our
students to the diverse intellectual traditions and cultures of Asia and the world.

name: Comenius University in Bratislava
description: The Faculty of Law at Comenius University in Bratislava has represented more than a 90-year-long period of co-existence of jurisprudence and legal education while using innovative and creative methods the primary objective of which is to prepare its graduates for the requirements of legal practice and to create high-quality academic works which ensure the development of practical application of law.

name: Stellenbosch University
description:
Stellenbosch University is a public research university situated in the town of Stellenbosch, South Africa. Other nearby universities are the University of Cape Town and University of the Western Cape.
Stellenbosch University (SU) is home to an academic community of 29 000 students (including 4 000 foreign students from 100 countries) as well as 3 000 permanent staff members (including 1 000 academics) on five campuses.
The main campus in the picturesque university town of Stellenbosch in the heart of the Western Cape winelands is quite an attraction for students. Stellenbosch is situated about 50 km from Cape Town and just 30 km from Cape Town International Airport.
SU has ten faculties: AgriSciences, Economic and Management Sciences, Medicine and Health Sciences, Engineering, Military Sciences, Arts and Social Sciences, Science, Education, Law and Theology.

name: University of Cape Town
description:
The University of Cape Town (UCT) is a public research university located in Cape Town in the Western Cape province of South Africa. UCT was founded in 1829 as the South African College making it the oldest higher education institute in South Africa. It is jointly the oldest university in South Africa and the oldest extant university in Sub-Saharan Africa alongside Stellenbosch University which received full university status on the same day in 1918.
UCT is the highest-ranked African university in the QS World University Rankings, the Times Higher Education World University Rankings, and the Academic Ranking of World Universities, and its Law and Commerce Faculties are consistently placed among the hundred best internationally. It is the only African member of the Global University Leaders Forum (GULF), within the World Economic Forum, which is made up of 26 of the world's top universities. The language of instruction is English.
UCT comprises of six faculties;
- Engineering & the Built Environment
- Health Sciences
- Science
- Commerce
- Law
- Humanities

name: Complutense University of Madrid
description:
The Universidad Complutense de Madrid (UCM), founded in 1293, is one of the oldest and most prestigious universities in Spain and Europe. With over 86,000 students and a wide range of academic disciplines, it is also one of the largest traditional (non-distance) universities in Europe. UCM is a public research university with a strong emphasis on academic excellence, social responsibility, and international collaboration. Its two main campuses—Moncloa and Somosaguas—are located in Madrid and offer students access to extensive libraries, research centers, and cultural facilities. The university has a long history of academic innovation and was among the first in the world to award doctoral degrees to women.
Madrid, the capital of Spain, offers a dynamic and student-friendly environment with a rich cultural heritage and excellent infrastructure. The city’s extensive public transport system—including metro, buses, and commuter trains—makes it easy for students to navigate between campuses and explore the city. Madrid is known for its world-class museums, lively neighborhoods, and green spaces like Retiro Park. A fun fact: Madrid is one of the highest capital cities in Europe, sitting at 667 meters above sea level, and its name is believed to come from the Arabic word
Magerit
, meaning “place of abundant water.” This blend of history, accessibility, and vibrant city life makes it an ideal destination for students.

name: Pompeu Fabra University
description:
Pompeu Fabra University (UPF), founded in 1990, is a modern public university located in the heart of Barcelona. It serves a student population of around 12,000 and is known for its strong focus on research, innovation, and internationalization. UPF offers programmes across social sciences, humanities, communication, health, and life sciences, and maintains a high level of academic performance and global engagement. The university emphasizes interdisciplinary learning and is closely connected to local and international research networks. Its compact urban campuses foster a dynamic and accessible academic environment.
Barcelona provides an ideal setting for student life, combining Mediterranean climate, rich cultural heritage, and excellent public transport. The city is known for its architecture, beaches, and vibrant neighborhoods, all easily reachable by metro, tram, or bike. Students benefit from a wide range of cultural events, cafés, and outdoor activities throughout the year. A fun fact: Barcelona is home to one of the few beaches in the world that was artificially created for the Olympics—before 1992, the city had no real beach culture. Today, it’s a central part of student life and a symbol of the city’s transformation.

name: Ramon Llull University
description:
ESADE is a global academic institution known for the quality of its education, its international outlook, and its focus on holistic personal development. ESADE has strong ties to the business world
ESADE Law School is Spain’s top private university for studying law and one of the most innovative law schools in the world. With more than thirty years of history, ESADE Law School is synonymous with excellence, an international focus, academic expertise and permanent connection with the professional world.

name: UNIVERSITY OF EXTREMADURA
description:
The Universidad de Extremadura (UEx), founded in 1973, is a public university serving the autonomous community of Extremadura in western Spain. It has a student population of over 20,000 and operates across four campuses located in Badajoz, Cáceres, Mérida, and Plasencia. UEx offers a wide range of academic disciplines and is known for its commitment to regional development through education, research, and innovation. The university maintains strong ties with local institutions and industries, and its facilities include libraries, laboratories, research centers, and sports complexes. Its structure and mission reflect a focus on accessibility, community engagement, and practical learning.
Extremadura offers a distinctive setting for student life, with a mix of historical towns, natural landscapes, and cultural traditions. The region is less crowded than other parts of Spain, making it ideal for students seeking a quieter and more immersive experience. Public transport connects the university campuses with surrounding cities and countryside, and students can explore UNESCO World Heritage sites, Roman ruins, and medieval architecture. A fun fact: Extremadura is the birthplace of many Spanish conquistadors, and cities like Medellín and Trujillo in Latin America are named after towns in the region. This historical legacy adds a unique dimension to studying in Extremadura.

name: Universidad de La Laguna
description:
The University of La Laguna, founded in 1792, is the oldest university in the Canary Islands and one of the most established in Spain. It serves a student population of around 20,000 and offers a broad range of academic disciplines across its faculties. The university is recognized for its commitment to research, particularly in areas related to marine sciences, astrophysics, and regional development. It maintains strong connections with local and international research networks and emphasizes practical learning and community engagement. The campus environment combines historic buildings with modern facilities, supporting both academic and extracurricular activities.
Located in San Cristóbal de La Laguna on the island of Tenerife, the university offers students a unique setting that blends historical heritage with a subtropical climate. The city is a UNESCO World Heritage site, known for its colonial architecture and vibrant student life. Public transport connects the campus with nearby beaches, mountains, and the island’s capital, Santa Cruz. A fun fact: Tenerife is home to Mount Teide, the highest peak in Spain and one of the world’s largest volcanoes, offering students opportunities for outdoor exploration alongside their studies.

name: Universidad de Salamanca
description:
The Universidad de Salamanca, founded in 1218, is the oldest university in Spain and one of the oldest in Europe. It serves a student population of around 30,000 and offers a comprehensive range of academic disciplines across its faculties. The university is renowned for its historical significance, academic excellence, and contributions to Spanish language and culture. It maintains a strong research profile and international presence, attracting students and scholars from around the world. The campus features a blend of historic architecture and modern facilities, providing a unique academic environment.
Salamanca is a vibrant university city in western Spain, known for its well-preserved medieval center and lively student atmosphere. The city is compact and walkable, with efficient public transport and a wide range of cultural events, cafés, and festivals. Students can explore historic landmarks, including the famous Plaza Mayor and the university’s ornate façade. A fun fact: Salamanca’s university is home to the “frog on the skull” carving, a symbol of good luck for students who find it on the university’s façade—a tradition that continues to attract visitors and students alike.

name: Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona
description:
The Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona (UAB), established in 1968, is a leading public university in Spain known for its strong research orientation and international outlook. It serves a student population of over 35,000 and offers a wide range of academic disciplines across its faculties. UAB is recognized for its interdisciplinary approach, innovative teaching methods, and close collaboration with research institutes and industry partners. The university’s main campus is designed as a self-contained academic community, providing students with access to modern facilities, libraries, and support services in a single location.
Located just outside Barcelona, UAB offers students the advantages of a campus environment while being close to one of Europe’s most dynamic cities. Barcelona is known for its rich cultural life, Mediterranean climate, and excellent public transport, making it easy for students to commute between the campus and the city. The region offers a mix of historic sites, beaches, and vibrant neighborhoods, providing a diverse and stimulating setting for student life.

name: UNIVERSITAT POLITÉCNICA DE VALÈNCIA
description:
The university dates back to the early 1970s. It is a public, dynamic, and innovative institution that is dedicated to researching and teaching. UPV maintains strong bonds with its social environment and a strong presence abroad.
Nearly 37,800 students are spread over UPV’s three campuses: Vera Campus (main campus) is located very close to the city centre, and it contains all of UPV’s science departments and schools.

name: University of A Coruña
description:
The University of A Coruña, established in 1989, is a public institution located in the region of Galicia in northwestern Spain. It serves a student population of around 20,000 and offers a wide range of academic disciplines across its faculties. The university is recognized for its commitment to research, particularly in fields such as engineering, environmental sciences, and social sciences. It maintains strong connections with local industries and international partners, emphasizing practical learning and innovation. The campus environment combines modern facilities with access to research centers and student support services.
A Coruña is a coastal city known for its maritime heritage, lively atmosphere, and student-friendly environment. The city offers efficient public transport, a walkable center, and easy access to beaches and green spaces. Students can enjoy a variety of cultural events, local cuisine, and historic landmarks such as the Tower of Hercules, a Roman lighthouse and UNESCO World Heritage site. A fun fact: The Tower of Hercules is the oldest working lighthouse in the world, and its image is featured on the city’s coat of arms.

name: University of Alicante
description:
The University of Alicante was created in October 1979 on the structure of the University Study Centre (CEU), which was started in 1968. The University main campus is located in San Vicente del Raspeig/Sant Vicent del Raspeig, bordering the city of Alicante to the north.
Universidad de Alicante offers a wide range of sports activities which becomes available with a university sports card (TDU). The facilities include gym, swimming pool, athletics track, squash courts, tatami, tennis and paddle courts, and table tennis.

name: University of Almeria
description:
The University of Almería, established in 1993, is a public university located on Spain’s southeastern Mediterranean coast. It serves around 13,000 students and offers a broad range of academic disciplines, with particular strengths in agricultural sciences, environmental studies, and biotechnology. The university is recognized for its research and innovation in sustainable agriculture and greenhouse technology, reflecting the region’s economic focus. Its modern campus provides students with advanced facilities, research centers, and a supportive academic environment.
Almería is a coastal city known for its sunny climate, beaches, and distinctive desert landscapes. The city offers a relaxed, student-friendly atmosphere, efficient public transport, and easy access to both the Mediterranean Sea and nearby natural parks. Students can enjoy cultural events, outdoor activities, and local cuisine. A fun fact: Almería’s Tabernas Desert is the only true desert in mainland Europe and has served as the filming location for numerous classic Western movies.

name: University of Barcelona
description:
The University of Barcelona, founded in 1450, is one of Spain’s largest and most prestigious public universities. It serves a student population of over 60,000 and offers a comprehensive range of academic disciplines across its faculties. The university is recognized for its strong research output, international collaborations, and commitment to academic excellence. Its campuses are integrated into the city, combining historic buildings with modern facilities and providing students with access to extensive libraries, research centers, and support services.
Barcelona offers a dynamic setting for student life, with a Mediterranean climate, rich cultural heritage, and efficient public transport. The city is known for its architecture, beaches, and vibrant neighborhoods, making it easy for students to balance academic pursuits with leisure and cultural activities. A fun fact: Barcelona’s main campus is located near the Eixample district, famous for its grid layout and iconic works by architect Antoni Gaudí, including the Sagrada Família and Casa Batlló.

name: University of Granada
description:
The University of Granada is the result of the adoption of the University Autonomy Act of 1983. The UGR is currently ranked among the world’s leading higher education institutions. The UGR vows to remain a university open to all, regardless of culture, creed or personal beliefs, and is fully committed to pioneering research, innovation, and delivering world-class education.
Approximately 80,000 individuals – students, researchers, lecturers, and administrative and service staff are directly linked to the UGR, making it the 4th largest university in the country.

name: University of Murcia
description:
The University of Murcia, founded in its modern form in 1915, is a public institution and the largest university in the Region of Murcia, serving approximately 38,000 students. It offers a wide range of academic disciplines across multiple campuses, including La Merced in the city center and Espinardo to the north. The university is known for its commitment to research, innovation, and regional development, with specialized campuses dedicated to health sciences, sports, and environmental studies. It maintains strong ties with local industries and international partners, and its facilities include research institutes, libraries, and cultural centers.
Murcia is a southeastern Spanish city known for its Mediterranean climate, historical architecture, and student-friendly atmosphere. The city offers affordable living, efficient public transport, and a relaxed pace of life, making it well-suited for academic study. Students can explore local markets, festivals, and nearby natural attractions such as the Mar Menor lagoon. A fun fact: Murcia is often called the “Garden of Europe” due to its extensive agricultural production, especially of fruits and vegetables, much of which is exported across the continent.

name: University of the Basque Country
description:
The University of the Basque Country is a 30-year-old institution with 45,000 students, 5,000 world-class academic staff and state-of-the-art facilities.
The university contains three campuses, one for each of the three provinces of the Basque Autonomous Community: Campus of Alava in Vitoria-Gasteiz, Campus of Biscay in Leioa and Bilbao and Campus of Gipuzkoa in Donostia-San Sebastián and Eibar.
Students are welcome to combine courses from different faculties; however, they should be aware of possible timetable conflicts.

name: University of Valencia
description:
The University of Valencia, founded in 1499, is one of Spain’s oldest and most prominent public universities. It serves a student population of over 60,000 and offers a wide range of academic disciplines across its faculties. The university is known for its strong research output, particularly in health sciences, environmental studies, and social sciences, and maintains active international collaborations. Its campuses—Blasco Ibáñez, Tarongers, and Burjassot-Paterna—are integrated into the city and provide students with access to modern facilities, libraries, and research centers.
Valencia is a Mediterranean city known for its blend of historical architecture, contemporary design, and student-friendly atmosphere. The city offers efficient public transport, including metro, tram, and bike-sharing systems, and is well-connected to beaches, parks, and cultural venues. Students can enjoy local festivals, such as Las Fallas, and explore the City of Arts and Sciences, a major architectural and cultural complex. A fun fact: Valencia is the birthplace of paella, one of Spain’s most iconic dishes, traditionally cooked over an open fire in wide, shallow pans.

name: Halmstad University
description:
Halmstad University conducts education and research within two profile areas, Health Innovation and Smart Cities and Communities, with a basis in three prominent doctoral education areas: Information Technology, Innovation Sciences, and Health and Lifestyle.
Today, the University has around 11,000 students (approximately 5,200 full-time students) and offers around 50 programmes and over 130 courses within several subject fields.

name: Karlstad University
description:
The Karlstad University is a dynamic and modern institution with around 19 000 students and a wide variety of programmes. Courses are primarily taught in Swedish, but there is a healthy selection of single courses in English, making it a solid option for exchange.
The city of Karlstad provides a friendly and manageable setting for student life with a nice walkable city centre. Karlstad campus is a few kilometers outside the city but is well connected through public transit. The broader region offers plenty of natural surroundings: Vänern lake, forests, rivers and outdoor options are all close by.

name: Karolinska Institutet
description:
Karolinska Institutet is one of Sweden’s most prominent medical universities, internationally recognized for its research and academic excellence in health sciences. With approximately 6,000 students and over 2,000 doctoral candidates, it maintains a focused academic environment supported by around 5,000 employees, including leading researchers and clinicians. The university is unique in that it is responsible for selecting Nobel laureates in Physiology or Medicine, a distinction that underscores its global influence in biomedical research. Its close integration with Stockholm’s healthcare system provides students with direct access to clinical environments and research facilities.
Located in the Stockholm region, Karolinska Institutet offers students the opportunity to live and study in one of Europe’s most technologically advanced and environmentally conscious capitals. The city combines efficient public transport, widespread English proficiency, and a strong cultural infrastructure, making it accessible and navigable for international students. Stockholm is built on 14 islands connected by over 50 bridges, and its proximity to forests and waterways allows for outdoor activities year-round. A small curiosity: the city’s metro system is often referred to as the world’s longest art gallery, with installations and sculptures integrated into nearly every station.

name: Linköping University
description:
At Linköping University you’ll find around 44 000 students across its multiple campuses. The institution is well known for its innovative education and interdisciplinary research, and you’ll find a strong selection of programmes and individual courses taught in English. The main campus is located a couple of kilometers outside of the city, giving a traditional university town atmosphere.
The city of Linköping and its nearby twin city Norrköping offer a student-friendly setting. Beyond the city you’ll have access to Swedish countryside, lakes, forests and peaceful nature reserves that are just a short trip away.

name: Linnæus University
description: Linnaeus University, established in 2010, is a state university located in Växjö and Kalmar, Sweden. Named after the renowned botanist Carl Linnaeus, the university offers a vibrant and inclusive campus environment. The Växjö campus has all teaching facilities within walking distance with a variety of programmes and single courses in English. The surroundings of Växjö are full of lakes, forests, and nature trails, making it easy to go hiking, swimming, or kayaking.

name: Luleå University of Technology
description:
Luleå University of Technology, located in the Arctic Region, has four campuses and over a hundred education programs. The university serves around 18,000 students. It offers programmes and courses in Swedish as the primary language of instruction, but it also has a growing number of courses in English.
The city of Luleå sits in Sweden’s far north and provides a distinctive Nordic student experience.
