The main campus lies within reach of the central city, and everyday necessities are accessible by local transit and cycling when the weather allows. Beyond the urban amenities you’ll find dramatic natural surroundings: forests, coastlines and snow in winter. For an exchange student willing to embrace the climate, Luleå offers both solid academic life and a memorable location.

name: Lund University
description:
Lund University is one of Scandinavia’s oldest and largest institutions, with a student population of over 45,000. It is internationally recognized for its research output and participation in major EU projects places it among the leading research universities in northern Europe. Its historical foundation in 1666 and continued emphasis on academic freedom distinguish it from other institutions. The university offers courses taught in both English and Swedish across a wide range of disciplines, making it highly accessible to students from all over the world.
The university is situated in the city of Lund in southern Sweden, a compact and walkable city with a strong student presence. Lund combines medieval architecture with modern research parks, and its size makes it easy for students to navigate daily life without relying on public transport.

name: Malmö University
description:
Malmö University is a relatively young institution, established in 1998, with a student population of around 24,000 and approximately 1,800 staff. It is known for its focus on urban studies, sustainability, and social innovation, and maintains strong connections with the surrounding community and regional industries. The university emphasizes interdisciplinary collaboration and internationalization, with a high proportion of students and faculty from outside Sweden. Its central location within Malmö allows for close integration with the city’s public services, cultural institutions, and business networks.
The university is located in Malmö, Sweden’s third-largest city, situated at the southern tip of the country and directly connected to Copenhagen via the Öresund Bridge. Malmö is compact, bike-friendly, and known for its diversity, with over 170 nationalities represented in the population. The city offers a mix of modern architecture, coastal parks, and historical sites, all within walking distance of the university. A small curiosity: Malmö’s Turning Torso is the tallest building in Scandinavia and was the first twisted skyscraper in the world.

name: Mid Sweden University
description:
Mid Sweden University is an inspiring and dynamic institution with campuses in Ôstersynd and Sundsvall. It has around 14 000 students and two main campuses, one in Sundsvall and one in Östersund. It offers courses taught in Swedish and a number of programmes and single-courses taught in English.
The city settings of the campuses give a great student experience in both Sundsvall and Östersund. You’ll find central neighbourhoods where cafés, shops and student services are within walking distance of campus and accommodation, making day-to-day life convenient. The surrounding region also offers access to nature with lakes, forests and hiking in summer or skiing in winter, so there’s a strong mix of urban and outdoor life.

name: Örebro University
description:
Örebro is situated a two hours’ drive west from Stockholm, in the heart of Sweden: Örebro is the 6th largest town in Sweden with a population of 150,000. It is a town with a historic atmosphere that is enhanced by the winter darkness, and it stands out in a colorful bloom in the spring. Close to nature, bike-friendly and full of culture – Örebro possesses qualities of both a larger city and a classic Swedish small town.
The School of Law in Örebro is combined with Psychology and Social Work studies. This exciting blend facilitates interaction, exchange of competencies and skills, and collaboration beyond subject boundaries. We are host to a number of strong research environments with prominent researchers, who are also involved in teaching at all levels.
As an exchange student at Örebro University, you will be a part of a modern, broad-based University with an ambitious vision - to lead towards a knowledge-driven society. You will also be invited to take part in a one-of-a-kind three week long orientation programme offering a variety of activities

name: Stockholm University
description:
Stockholm University, established in 1878 as a college and granted university status in 1960, is a renowned public research university located in Stockholm, Sweden. With its rich history and academic excellence, the university attracts over 33,000 students, making it one of the largest universities in Scandinavia. The university comprises four faculties offering a wide range of academic programs. Situated in the world's first national urban park, the campus blends seamlessly with nature, architecture, and modern art, providing a unique and inspiring learning environment. The main campus, Frescati, is conveniently located near an underground railway station, facilitating easy access for students.
Stockholm is spread across islands connected by bridges, offering picturesque views of waterways, parks and historic architecture. It’s an easy city to navigate on foot with a lively cultural scene including museums, concerts, cafes and festivals. The surroundings offer easy access to forests, lakes and the Stockholm Archipelago with thousands of islands just a short boat trip away.

name: Swedish School of Sport and Health Sciences
description:
The Swedish School of Sport and Health Sciences, GIH, (formerly Stockholm University College of Physical Education and Sports) was founded in 1813, which makes it the oldest University College in the world within its field.
GIH offers degree programmes preparing for the teaching profession in Physical Education as well as for a career in Sports Coaching, Sport Management or Preventive Health.
GIH is part of the rich research environment in Stockholm which includes Karolinska Institutet, Stockholm University and KTH Royal Institute of Technology.

name: Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences (SLU)
description:
Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences (SLU) is a young university with a long history. It was founded in 1977 out of the agricultural, forestry and veterinary university colleges, the Veterinary School at Skara and the Forestry School at Skinnskatteberg.
SLU has three main campuses: Alnarp, Umeå and Uppsala.

name: Umeå University
description:
The Umeå University is one of Sweden’s leading comprehensive universities, with over 40 000 students enrolled. It offers a large number of programmes and courses taught in English, making it an attractive option for exchange students. The university is known for its strong research and for fostering an open and collaborative academic environment.
The city of Umeå provides a friendly and accessible setting for student life, with a compact and walkable central area where cafés, shops and cultural venues are easily reachable from campus. Beyond the urban environment you’ll find vast natural surroundings: forests, rivers, hiking and bike paths and plenty of snow in winter.

name: University of Gothenburg
description:
The University of Gothenburg, founded in 1891, is one of Sweden’s largest and most respected universities, with around 58,000 students. It offers a broad academic portfolio across eight faculties with plenty of elements available in English. The university is renowned for its high-quality research often ranking among the top 200 universities worldwide. The university does not sit on one single sprawling campus; instead its faculties and departments are spread across a number of major locations within the city of Gothenburg
Living in Gothenburg adds to the appeal. Sweden’s second-largest city, with about 600,000 residents, combines a lively urban environment with the relaxed feel of a coastal town. Students enjoy the city’s canals, green spaces, vibrant music and food scenes, and excellent public transport that makes exploring easy. Meanwhile, there are plenty of outdoor possibilities, including quick escapes to the nearby archipelago.

name: Uppsala University
description:
Established in 1477, Uppsala University is the oldest and prestigious university in Sweden and the Nordic region. Located in Uppsala, it offers a wide range of academic disciplines across its nine faculties, including the renowned Faculty of Law. With a strong emphasis on research and international collaboration, the Faculty of Law provides a vibrant research environment and highly regarded legal education. The unique training model and active involvement of prominent researchers ensure high-quality education and enriching research experiences for students. The university's historic legacy and commitment to excellence make it a sought-after destination for students and scholars alike.
With about 52,000 students in a compact city of just over 230,000 residents, Uppsala has a uniquely youthful atmosphere where bikes outnumber cars and student life shapes much of the local culture. The city is known for its beautiful river views, historic university buildings, and cozy cafés that fill with students studying or socializing. A big part of life here revolves around the traditional student “nations”—13 social clubs that organize everything from formal dinners and choirs to club nights and themed parties, making it easy to meet people and dive into Swedish traditions. Despite being a historic city, Uppsala feels dynamic and international, offering plenty of cultural events, outdoor activities, and excellent train connections to Stockholm just 40 minutes away.

name: ETH Zurich
description:
Established in 1855 as the Federal Polytechnical School, ETH Zurich has from the outset been a national centre for education with international appeal, attracting talent from all over the world.
Today, ETH Zurich is one of the leading international universities for technology and the natural sciences. It is well known for its excellent education, ground-breaking fundamental research and for implementing its results directly into practice.
ETH Zurich has more than 18,500 students from over 110 countries. 21 Nobel Laureates have studied, taught or conducted research at ETH Zurich, underlining the excellent reputation of the university.

name: UNIVERSITY OF NEUCHATEL
description:
Université de Neuchâtel is a public university in western Switzerland with a student body of approximately 4,000 and a staff of around 1,200. It offers a compact academic environment with four faculties and a strong emphasis on research, particularly in law, economics, and natural sciences. The university is known for its bilingual setting (French and English), which supports international collaboration and mobility. Its manageable size allows for close interaction between students and faculty, and its location in the French-speaking part of Switzerland provides access to cross-border academic networks.
The university is located in the city of Neuchâtel, situated on the shores of Lake Neuchâtel and surrounded by the Jura mountains. The city is known for its watchmaking heritage and offers a mix of historical architecture and natural landscapes. Neuchâtel is walkable, well-connected by rail, and offers a calm setting for study with access to outdoor activities year-round. A small curiosity: the lake next to the city is the largest entirely within Swiss borders, and its water is so clear that it’s used as a benchmark for measuring lake transparency across Europe.

name: University of Bern
description:
The University of Bern, founded in 1834, is one of Switzerland’s leading comprehensive universities, enrolling around 19,000 students across eight faculties and offering a wide spectrum of programs in the humanities, natural sciences, law, economics, medicine, and social sciences. With a strong focus on interdisciplinary research, sustainability, and global cooperation, the university ranks among the top 120–200 universities worldwide, depending on the field. It is particularly renowned for cutting-edge research in climate science, space, and health. Students benefit from close links to governmental institutions and international organizations located in Bern, providing unique opportunities for internships, networking, and real-world projects.
Living in Bern as a student means enjoying all the advantages of Switzerland’s picturesque capital city. With its UNESCO-listed medieval Old Town, lively café culture, and riverside spots along the Aare for swimming or relaxing, Bern combines a laid-back atmosphere with rich cultural offerings. The university’s facilities are mostly concentrated in the welcoming Länggasse district, where student life thrives thanks to numerous associations, events, and support services like the Welcome Center and student union. Excellent public transport, bike-friendly streets, and proximity to the Alps make it easy to explore both the city and Switzerland’s stunning natural landscapes, offering an outstanding quality of life alongside your studies.

name: University of Geneva
description:
Situated between the Alps and the Jura mountains, at the southwestern tip of Switzerland and Lake Geneva, Geneva is in the heart of Western Europe. Its ideal geographical location has made the city a prosperous hub for trade and exchanges of all kinds.
This cosmopolitan city is home to more than 180 nationalities and is recognized worldwide for its spirit of openness and tolerance.
Considered the smallest of the major world capitals, Geneva, which is home to some thirty international organizations including the UN, WTO, WHO and ILO and more than 300 NGOs and permanent missions of foreign states, has a true international vocation.This multicultural environment is reflected at the University of Geneva, where about one third of the students are foreign nationals. The university pursues a very active policy of international relations; in particular, it participates in numerous bi- or multilateral agreements, networks and programs such as Erasmus and Socrates.
Ideally located near the most famous ski areas of the Alps, not far from the Mediterranean, while being anchored in Central Europe,
Geneva
offers the rare advantages of a cosmopolitan city on a human scale. Cuisine and music from all over the world are found here. Lovers of green spaces will find an atmosphere conducive to meditation in its parks or on the shores of Lake Geneva.
Culture
lovers will be spoilt for choice, thanks to the presence in Geneva of one of the most prestigious
opera scenes
in Europe, several
film festivals
, and numerous concert halls and theaters.
The University of Geneva takes an active part in this cultural scene. Its film club and choir in particular attract large audiences. But Geneva also lives to the rhythm of a multitude of associations, representing the most diverse countries and interests, which make it uniquely suited for the exchange of ideas and traditions.

name: University of Lucerne
description:
The Faculty of Law at the University of Lucerne is the youngest law faculty in Switzerland. Since October 2001, it offers a curriculum based on the Bologna Model. Since then, the Lucerne University Faculty of Law has experienced an increase in popularity and number of students.
The Lucerne Faculty of Law offers an accomplished and prestigious program, which provides students with excellent opportunities in the job market, teaches skills essential for internships and work, and prepares them to score high (above average) on the Cantonal lawyer’s exams.

name: University of Zurich
description:
The University of Zurich (UZH), founded in 1833, is the largest university in Switzerland, enrolling around 28,000 students and supported by roughly 3,700 full‑time faculty
.
It offers the broadest range of subjects of any Swiss higher education institution, with seven faculties covering medicine, law, economics, natural sciences, humanities, theology, and veterinary medicine
.
UZH is internationally recognized for cutting‑edge research in life sciences, biomedical studies, climate science, and social sciences - featuring leading institutes such as the Institute of Molecular Life Sciences - and encourages a strong interdisciplinary approach
.
About 25% of students come from abroad, creating a vibrant multicultural academic environment with many research partnerships and study programs open to international applicants
.
Living in Zurich as a student means immersing yourself in a cosmopolitan yet manageable city with excellent transport and abundant social opportunities. Zurich’s well‑connected public transport and bike‑friendly streets make getting around easy, with student discounts available
.
Campus life is dynamic - UZH’s Academic Sports Association (ASVZ) offers over 120 sports activities, while the student union (VSUZH) and a dozen-plus associations organize academic, cultural, and political events
.
International students can join clubs ranging from acapella ensembles and environmental groups to investment clubs and political societies
.
Although Zurich’s cost of living is high, many students find shared flats through WOKO or nearby towns, and experience suggests that engagement in sports and social events helps with integration, even for those new to German
. Overall, UZH offers a rich blend of top-tier academics, diverse extracurriculars, and Swiss urban life steeped in culture and connection.

name: Bahcesehir University
description:
Bahçeşehir University (BAU) is a private institution in Istanbul, Turkey, with over 24,000 students and around 1,900 staff. Founded in 1998, it has developed a strong international profile, with more than 6,000 international students and over 290 global academic agreements. The university operates multiple campuses in Istanbul and maintains branch campuses in Berlin, Rome, Toronto, and Washington, D.C. BAU is notable for its CO-OP education model, which integrates academic study with professional internships through partnerships with over 2,300 companies. It ranks among the top Turkish universities in international outlook and sustainability.
The university is located in central Istanbul, with its main campus along the Bosphorus in Beşiktaş, offering students direct access to one of Europe’s most dynamic urban environments. Istanbul combines historical depth with modern infrastructure, and its extensive public transport network makes commuting between campuses and city districts efficient. The city’s cultural diversity and strategic location between Europe and Asia provide a unique setting for international exchange. A small curiosity: Istanbul is the only city in the world that spans two continents, with the Bosphorus Strait dividing its European and Asian sides.

name: Boğaziçi University
description:
Boğaziçi University, located in Istanbul, is one of Turkey’s most prestigious public universities, known for its strong academic programs and vibrant international community. Established in 1863 as Robert College and transformed into a public university in 1971, Boğaziçi offers a wide range of programs across six faculties, including Arts and Sciences, Economics and Administrative Sciences, Engineering, and Education. Exchange students can choose from a variety of English-taught courses, benefiting from a rigorous academic environment that emphasizes critical thinking, research, and a global perspective. The university’s longstanding tradition of academic excellence and its openness to international collaboration make it an ideal destination for students seeking a high-quality study abroad experience.
The university's main campus is situated on a hill overlooking the Bosphorus, providing a stunning backdrop for student life. Istanbul itself is a dynamic metropolis that bridges Europe and Asia, offering a rich blend of history, culture, and modern urban energy. Exchange students will find endless opportunities to explore the city’s historic landmarks, vibrant arts scene, and diverse culinary traditions, all while being part of a lively student community at Boğaziçi.

name: İstanbul Bilgi University
description:
Istanbul Bilgi University, established in 1996, is a leading foundation university in Turkey known for its innovative approach to education and strong international outlook. The university offers programs across various fields, including economics, business, law, communication, engineering, architecture, social sciences, and arts. Exchange students can choose from a wide range of English-taught courses, benefiting from an interdisciplinary academic environment that emphasizes critical thinking, creativity, and real-world application. Bilgi’s strong ties with industry, NGOs, and international partners provide students with opportunities for research, internships, and collaborative projects, making it an attractive destination for those seeking a dynamic academic experience in Istanbul.
With campuses located in central parts of Istanbul, including the iconic Santral Istanbul Campus, Bilgi offers students a vibrant learning environment within one of the world’s most historically rich and culturally diverse cities. Exchange students can enjoy exploring Istanbul’s unique blend of ancient landmarks, contemporary art scenes, bustling markets, and diverse culinary traditions. The university’s urban campuses are well-connected to the city’s cultural and social life, allowing students to immerse themselves fully in the dynamic rhythm of Istanbul.

name: İstanbul University
description:
Istanbul University is the oldest university in Turkey and one of the ten oldest universities in Europe, with a rich academic heritage dating back to 1453 following the conquest of Constantinople by Sultan Mehmet the Conqueror. Today, the university serves more than 250,000 students across 16 faculties, 17 institutes, and numerous research centers. Exchange students can access a wide range of academic disciplines, including humanities, social sciences, law, economics, science, and medicine, benefiting from the university’s strong academic traditions and its role as a leading institution in Turkish higher education. The university’s central location and large academic community offer an enriching environment for learning and cultural exchange.
Located in the heart of Istanbul, the Beyazıt Campus is surrounded by the city’s historical and cultural landmarks, providing students with a unique backdrop for their studies. From the Grand Bazaar and Hagia Sophia to the vibrant neighborhoods along the Bosphorus, students have countless opportunities to explore Istanbul’s rich heritage and dynamic urban life. The city’s blend of Eastern and Western influences, combined with its status as Turkey’s economic and cultural hub, makes it an exciting and immersive destination for international students.

name: Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv
American University in Dubai (AUD)
description:
In 1995, Mr. Bou Saab officially established the American University in Dubai, with the full commitment and support of H.H. Sheikh Mohammed Bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice President and Prime Minister of the UAE, Ruler of Dubai.
The American University in Dubai is a fully independent, vibrant institution which serves as a point of reference for higher education within the Gulf Region and greater Middle East. It currently educates more than 2,000 students of more than100 nationalities, and remains the first institution outside of the U.S. and Latin America to receive accreditation from the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges (SACSCOC).

name: Aberystwyth University
description:
Aberystwyth University was the first university in Wales and is an established traditional university, founded in 1872. The university welcomes students from all parts of the EU and has strong links with Denmark. It is recognised as leading in the field of research for Computer Science, the Arts, Political Studies, Environmental Sciences, Creative Writing, Theatre and Performance and Celtic and Medieval History.
Aberystwyth University welcomes well over 100 exchange students from over 15 countries around Europe into a wide range of academic departments.

name: Goldsmiths, University of London
description:
Goldsmiths was founded in 1891 and has been part of the University of London since 1904 – being a creative powerhouse with a rich academic heritage. Today, Goldsmiths has a close-knit community, with students and staff from around the world who are inventive, imaginative and original. Goldsmiths offers a range of undergraduate and postgraduate study options in the arts, humanities, social sciences, cultural studies, computing, and entrepreneurial business and management, all on a friendly, accessible, single-site campus.
At just a 10-minute train ride from London Bridge, it’s easy to access all central London has to offer, while being based in a vibrant and diverse local area.

name: Imperial College London
description:
As the UK’s only university focusing entirely on science, engineering, medicine and business, Imperial College London is truly unique, and in the QS World University Rankings 2022 came in at number 7.
Founded in 1907, Imperial’s expertise now spreads across nine campuses – six medical campuses, the centre for ecology, evolution, and conservation at Silwood Park, and White City Campus, the new 25-acre base for researchers, businesses and healthcare experts to work alongside each other.

name: KEELE UNIVERSITY
description: Kelle University is located in the UK county of North Strffordshire, midway between Birmingham and Manchester. The University is sorrounded by woods, lakes and parkland.

name: King's College London
description:
King's is one of the UK's most historic and prestigious universities founded in 1829.
With a forward thinking vision and state-of-the-art facilities, King's is renowned for excellence in both its innovative teaching and pioneering research.
Based in the heart of central London, and spread across five London campuses, King's is one of the largest multi-faculty institutions in the UK with more than 33,000 students.

name: Newcastle University
description: Newcastle University was founded in 1834 to educate the pioneers of the industrial revolution. Teaching was then, and is still, at the heart of the University: at Newcastle they educate for life, to develop and nurture successive generations of creative practitioners, clinicians, scientists, engineering and educationalists, and set them on the path to make their own mark on society.

name: Queen Mary University of London
description:
Queen Mary University was established in the nineteenth century, and it was founded to provide education to working class people living in London’s East End. Today, the university is known as a place that promote diversity and as they say, “a place where people of all classes and conditions congregate”. The university has more than 32,000 students.
The Mile End campus is home to most of the academic Schools and offers shops, cafés, restaurants, a gym and the 24-hour library. There’s plenty of green and outdoor space, but you’re only minutes away from Central London’s bustling streets.

name: Queen's University Belfast
description:
One of the leading universities in the UK and Ireland with a distinguished heritage and history. Founded in 1845 as Queen's College Belfast, it became an independent university in 1908.
Today, the university is ranked 198 in the world (Times Higher Education World University Rankings 2023), and is a member of the Russell Group of UK research intensive universities, combining excellence in research and education with a student-centred ethos.

name: UNIVERSITY OF BIRMINGHAM
description: The University of Birmingham has been challenging and developing great minds for more than a century. Characterised by a tradition of innovation, research at the university has broken new ground, pushed forward the boundaries of knowledge and made an impact on people’s lives. The university has been welcoming international students onto its campus since its inception in 1900 – and with over 5,000 international students from over 150 different countries, it has one of the largest and most vibrant international student communities in the UK.

name: UNIVERSITY OF BRISTOL
description: The University of Bristol has had a reputation for innovation since its founding in 1876. With a choice of over 200 degree courses covering a broad range of subjects, students at the University of Bristol engage with intellectually challenging courses that encourage independence of mind. The diversity of a centre for cutting-edge art, music and culture, coupled with being a historical city surrounded by countryside, make studying at Bristol a rich and exciting experience. Right in the heart of the city are many University buildings and facilities.

name: University of Edinburgh
description: From Nobel laureates and Olympic champions to space explorers and prime ministers, the University of Edinburgh (UoE) has been influencing history since it opened the gates to its first students in 1583. The university, which is in the center of Edinburgh, has approx. 41,000 students with over 18,000 international students from more than 150 countries. The city of Edinburgh enjoys a pedestrian- and cyclist-friendly infrastructure and offers good traffic links.

name: UNIVERSITY OF GLASGOW
description:
The University of Glasgow has been changing the world since 1451. The university has around 43,000 students and welcomes students from more than 140 countries worldwide. It is a world top 100 university and a member of the prestigious Russell Group of leading UK research universities.
T
he University of Glasgow
works with companies and organisations throughout the city to co-design solutions to create real, lasting impact and opportunity in Glasgow and beyond.
Its staff and students are engaged in strong, enduring research and community partnerships to improve health,
boost
the economy
, build a better future
and
celebrate
the achievements of those living in Glasgow.

name: UNIVERSITY OF KENT
description:
Kent Law School is one of the UK’s leading law schools. We have a distinctive critical approach, placing law within the wider context of society. Recognised excellence in teaching, world-class research, and an award-winning law clinic create an intellectually stimulating environment in which to study the law.
Kent Law School is based on the Canterbury campus, which is set in 300 acres of parkland. Everything you need is within walking distance. You can watch a play or a film at the Gulbenkian arts centre, dance at The Venue nightclub, keep fit at our sports centre and meet friends at one of many campus cafés and restaurants.
The campus is a 25-minute walk from Canterbury, a lovely city with a world-famous cathedral, medieval buildings, lively pubs and restaurants and a wide range of shops. There’s a vibrant cultural scene, including an annual arts festival, and the coast and countryside are within easy reach. London is less than an hour away by high-speed train.

name: THE UNIVERSITY OF LEEDS
description: The university of Leeds, which was founded in 1904, has around 32,000 students, making it one of the largest in the UK. In addition to study programmes in the humanities, the university also offers study programmes in the health sciences, natural sciences, social sciences, business economics, law and the technical sciences.

name: UNIVERSITY OF LEICESTER
description:
The University of Leicester was founded in 1921 as a memorial for all local people who made sacrifices during the First World War.
At the heart of the UK, Leicester is a leading university committed to international excellence, world-changing research and high quality, inspirational teaching. Celebrating diversity among our staff and students; widening participation in higher education; engaging with local, national and international communities – all of these are part of what we do and who we are.

name: University of Manchester
description: The University of Manchester is part of the prestigious Russell Group of universitites, with outstanding facilities and a wide range of courses. They are highly respected across the globe as a centre of teaching excellence and innovative research.

name: University of Nottingham
description:
The University of Nottingham is a public research university in Nottingham, United Kingdom. It was founded as University College Nottingham in 1881 and was granted a royal charter in 1948. The University of Nottingham belongs to the elite research-intensive Russell Group association.
Nottingham is organized into five constituent faculties, within which there are more than 50 schools, departments, institutes, and research centers. Nottingham has about 45,500 students from more than 150 countries.
The Students' Union hosts over 200 student societies. Choose from hobbies, sports and volunteering. There are cultural, national, and religious societies, providing a way to connect with other students

name: UNIVERSITY OF SHEFFIELD
description:
The University grew out of the Sheffield Medical School (founded in 1828), Firth College (1879) and the Sheffield Technical School (1884). These three institutions came together in 1897 to form the University College of Sheffield, which in turn became the University of Sheffield in 1905.
The University of Sheffield is a member of the prestigious Russell Group, and has a proud history of discovery, innovation and social change.
Sheffield is the 4th largest city in England and one of the safest & most low-cost cities.

name: UNIVERSITY OF ST ANDREWS
description:
Founded in 1413, the University of St Andrews is Scotland’s oldest university.
Studying at St Andrews offers the opportunity to learn at a university with high-quality educational experience in a safe, historic, and welcoming setting.
St Andrews has a diverse community that is home to over 9,000 students from more than 130 territories world-wide, offering global perspectives on you subject in a unique Scottish setting.

name: UNIVERSITY OF STIRLING
description:
Founded by Royal Charter in 1967, the University of Stirling was the first genuinely new university in Scotland for over 400 years. The pioneering spirit and a passion for innovation and excellence in all they do, is retained.
At the geographical heart of Scotland, Stirling naturally has superb links to the rest of the country and beyond. In particular, Edinburgh and Glasgow are both less than an hour away by road or rail and the Scottish Highlands are less than an hour away to the north.

name: University of Warwick
description:
The university was founded in 1965 as part of a government initiative to expand higher education. It has been a mark of Warwick's strategy to encourage and facilitate admission from those less well-advantaged and from poorer backgrounds.
The university has around 29,500 full-time students. The university is located outside the city of Coventry, England - close to Birmingham.

name: UNIVERSITY OF YORK
description: The University of York is situated on a beautiful parkland campus close to one of Britain’s most historic cities. Established in 1963, the university has expanded to more than thirty departments and centers, covering a wide range of subjects. The University has just below 19,000 students and places an emphasis on small class sizes, personal attention and guidance. The university has a lively, cosmopolitan campus with its own shops, banks, bars and restaurants.

name: Arizona State University
description: The university was founded in 1885 and is among the largest universities in the US with more than 74,000 students from 120 countries. ASU has four campuses located throughout the Phoenix metropolitan area, but are easily accessible by free intercampus shuttles. While international exchange students can study at any campus, most take courses at the Tempe campus due to the high number of classes and programs offered. Tempe is a lively university city, only a five-minute drive from Phoenix.

name: Barnard College
description:
Barnard College of Columbia University was founded in 1889 and is devoted to empowering young women to pursue their passions. The Barnard community supports a community of 2,600 undergraduate women, all gathered on Campus Morningside Heights, situated in the heart of upper Manhattan.
The exchange agreement with Barnard is between DIS Copenhagen and Barnard College, and the exchange spots have been given to the University of Copenhagen by DIS. Students exchanged through the agreement should expect to attend an information meeting at DIS Copenhagen where you will meet students from Barnard studying in Copenhagen.

name: Boston College
description: Boston College was founded in 1863 and has an enrollment of nearly 14,700 students from more than 80 countries. BC is located in the residential neighborhood of Chestnut Hill, approximately 7 miles west of Boston. There are several tramlines into downtown Boston directly across from the campus as well as bus routes.

name: Boston University
description: Boston University was established in 1869 and offers a breadth of programs through its 17 Schools and Colleges. With more than 30,000 students from 140 countries, it is the fourth largest independent university in the US. Campus is located approximately 20 minutes from downtown Boston and offers more than 500 student clubs.

name: Cornell University
description: Cornell University is the federal land-grant institution of New York State, a private endowed university, a member of the Ivy League, and a partner of the State University of New York. It has been described as the first truly American university because of its founders' revolutionarily egalitarian and practical vision of higher education, and is dedicated to its land-grant mission of outreach and public service. Founded in 1865 by Ezra Cornell and Andrew Dickson White, Cornell was intended to teach and make contributions in all fields of knowledge. These ideals are captured in Cornell's motto, a popular 1865 Ezra Cornell quotation: "I would found an institution where any person can find instruction in any study."

name: Dartmouth College
facultyContact:
Nestled in the idyllic Northeast woods region of the United States sits the small town of Hanover, New Hampshire. Our vibrant, buzzing, global community was founded in 1769 on traditional, unceded Abenaki homelands.
Dartmouth is a fusion of a renowned liberal arts college and a robust research university. The unique quarter-system consists of four 10-week academic terms per year that align with the four seasons. With more than 60 areas of study, these seemingly different disciplines become natural partners.

name: Houston Methodist Hospital – Texas Medical Center
Montana State University
description: Founded in 1893, Montana State University-Bozeman has approximately 15,000 students including undergraduates and graduates Bozeman is situated in a valley in the Rocky Mountains. Outdoor activities include hiking, skiing, snowboarding, rock climbing, and mountain biking. MSU offers plenty of clubs and sports programs for students to participate in.

name: New York University
description:
Founded in 1831, New York University is one of the largest private universities in the United States. The University, which includes 18 schools, colleges and institutes, occupies five major centers in New York City. There are more than 50,000 students enrolled in all of the schools.
The center of NYU is the Washington Square campus in the heart of Greenwich Village. One of the city's most creative and energetic communities, the Village is a historic neighborhood that has attracted generations of writers, musicians, artists, and intellectuals. Beyond the Village, New York City becomes an extension of the University's campus. In addition to its Manhattan locations, the University is also located in Brooklyn with the second oldest school of engineering and technology in the country, and has numerous research facilities.

name: North Carolina State University
description: North Carolina State University is a pre-eminent research enterprise that excels in science, technology, engineering, math, design, the humanities and social sciences, textiles and veterinary medicine. With more than 35,000 students and nearly 8,000 faculty and staff, NC State University transforms lives and provides leadership for social, economic, and technological development across North Carolina and around the world. Approximately 4,800 international students are currently enrolled at NC State, and the international students and faculty represent over 120 countries. The university is within two hours of the Atlantic Ocean, and within three hours of the Blue Ridge Mountains. The area offers numerous opportunities for hiking, camping, surfing, boating and various other activities.

name: Purdue University
description:
Founded in 1869, Purdue is situated between Chicago (193 km northwest), the third largest city in the United States, and Indianapolis (105 km southeast), home of the Indy 500 motor race and capital of Indiana.
The West Lafayette campus offers more than 200 majors for undergraduates, over 70 master’s and doctoral programs, and professional degrees in pharmacy and veterinary medicine. In addition, it has 18 intercollegiate sports teams and more than 850 student organizations.
Discover your world by studying abroad at Purdue in West Lafayette, Indiana.

name: UC Law SF
description: This school used to be called UC Hastings College of Law, but had a name change in July 2023: https://uclawsf.edu/new-name/

name: University of Arizona
description: The University of Arizona in Tucson was established in 1885 and supports a community of 47,000 students. As one of the largest public institutions in its state, UA offers a wide range of activities and academic opportunities to its students. The main campus is located in the city of Tucson near several famous parks and mountains.

name: University of California, Davis
description:
At UC Davis School of Law, the curriculum is designed to provide a solid foundation of practical knowledge and skills that enable our graduates to pursue careers in whatever area of legal practice they may choose, from public service to business litigation to legal scholarship.
Each of our faculty members is truly committed to teaching and together they offer a challenging academic program with diverse specialities including but not limited to business law, environmental law, international and comparative law, intellectual property law, immigration law, constitutional law and public interest law.

name: University of Colorado Boulder
description:
CU Boulder was founded in 1876 and supports a community of over 30,000 students. The university is situated at the foot of the Rocky Mountains with miles of biking and hiking trails and close proximity to skiing. The student recreation center has rock-climbing, ice-skating, swimming, tennis, weight room, racquetball courts and much more.
The exchange agreement with CU Boulder is between DIS Copenhagen and CU Boulder, and the exchange spots have been given to the University of Copenhagen by DIS. Students exchanged through the agreement should expect to attend an information meeting at DIS Copenhagen where you will meet students from CU Boulder studying in Copenhagen.

name: University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign
description:
Illinois Industrial University was founded in 1867 and opened on year later in 1868. In 1885 the university was renamed The University of Illinois.
The university is in the twin cities of Champaign and Urbana (total population 207,000) in east-central Illinois. Situated about 140 miles south of Chicago, 125 miles west of Indianapolis, and 180 miles northeast of St. Louis.
49,339 students are enrolled at the university, which includes 5,270 international students from 78 countries.

name: University of Kansas
description: The university was founded in 1864 and has more than 25,000 students including about 1600 international students. The main campus is situated in Mount Oread, Lawrence. KU also has two other campuses nearby: The University of Kansas Medical Center in Kansas City (approximately 41 miles from the main campus) and the Edwards Campus in Overland Park (approximately 34 miles from the main campus). However, almost all of the classes for exchange students will be on the main campus in Lawrence.

name: University of Miami
description: University of Miami is a private research university with more than 16,000 students from around the world, located in Coral Gables, FL, a suburb of Miami. The campus has about 10,000 undergraduate students and is very lively. Students can become involved in organizations, clubs, and sports during their exchange program.

name: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
description: The university is the nation's first public university, founded in 1789, and supports a community of more than 30,000 students. UNC Chapel Hill has one campus, located in Chapel Hill's downtown area, encompassing the Morehead Planetarium and the many shops on Franklin Street. UNC Chapel Hill Students can participate in over 550 officially student organizations.

name: University of North Carolina at Charlotte
description: The University was founded in 1946 and supports a community of over 30,000 students. UNC Charlotte is the largest institution of higher education in the Charlotte region. UNC Charlotte has three campuses: Charlotte Research Institute Campus, Center City Campus, and the main campus, located in University City. The Charlotte 49ers offers 18 division 1 sports, making the athletic facilities very popular.

name: University of North Carolina at Greensboro
description:
University of North Carolina Greensboro is a public institution, founded in 1891. UNCG is located in the central part of the state, about midway between Washington and Atlanta.
The University supports a community of 20,000 students and has an architecturally diverse campus with distinctively unique landmarks.

name: University of San Diego
description:
The University of San Diego School of Law is recognized for the excellence of its faculty, depth of its curriculum and strength of its clinical programs.
Each year, USD educates approximately 800 Juris Doctor and graduate law students from throughout the United States and around the world. The law school is best known for its offerings in the areas of business and corporate law, constitutional law, intellectual property, international and comparative law, public interest law and taxation.
USD School of Law is one of the 84 law schools elected to the Order of the Coif, a national honor society for law school graduates. The law school's faculty is a strong group of outstanding scholars and teachers with national and international reputations and currently ranks in the top 20% (36th out of 204) among U.S. law schools in scholarly impact according to a 2018 study. The school is accredited by the American Bar Association and is a member of the Association of American Law Schools. Founded in 1954, the law school is part of the University of San Diego, a private, independent, Roman Catholic university chartered in 1949.

name: University of South Florida
description:
The university was founded in 1956 and support a community of almost 50,000 students. USF is
situated in the vibrant and diverse Tampa Bay region with campuses in Tampa, St. Petersburg
and Sarasota-Manatee. USF Intercollegiate Athletics is home to 17 men's and women's teams,
including football, basketball, baseball, softball and soccer, competing at the NCAA level.

name: University of the Pacific
description:
The University of the Pacific, McGeorge School of Law has grown into an internationally recognized leader in the field of legal education since its establishment in 1924. Its location in Sacramento, the capital of California, has shaped its focus on public law, international law and advocacy.
Our success is built on a distinguished faculty, high quality students, committed and involved alumni, and a beautiful, spacious campus with state-of-the art classrooms and student facilities.
Yet it is also built on vision. McGeorge is an institution on the move, a dynamic law school that is changing and growing to meet the challenges of the global economy and to educate the lawyers who will be tomorrow’s leaders.

name: University of Washington
description:
University of Washington is a public institution founded in 1861. Located in the University
District neighborhood (known as the U District) just north of downtown Seattle, the university
supports a community of more than 54,000 students. UW is a multi-campus university in
Seattle, Tacoma and Bothell. Tacoma and Bothell is approximately 20-30 minutes from
downtown Seattle, but can be easily reached by bus.

name: University of Wisconsin-Madison
description:
UW-Madison has long been recognized as one of America’s great universities, regularly ranked as one of the top public research universities in the United States.
Many of UW-Madison’s academic programs are ranked among the best in the nation with 9000+ courses and 400+ degree programs. A public, land-grant institution, UW-Madison offers a complete spectrum of humanities, social science, business, science, and engineering courses.
Madison is the capital of Wisconsin and one of the hubs of education, business, and culture in the state, known for a vibrant entertainment and performing arts scene.
Madison residents are active, and spend time in parks, on bike paths, and in and around Madison’s four lakes. Madison has frequently been ranked as one of the best places to live in the United States.

name: Vermont Law and Graduate School
description:
Vermont Law and Graduate School, a private, independent institution, is home to a law school that offers ABA-accredited residential and online hybrid JD programs and a graduate school that offers master’s degrees and certificates in multiple disciplines, including programs offered by the Maverick
Lloyd School for the Environment, the Center for Justice Reform and other graduate-level programs emphasizing the intersection of environmental justice, social justice, and public policy. Both the law and graduate schools strongly feature experiential clinical and field work learning. For more information, visit vermontlaw.edu and the Interactive Viewbook which includes information about the campus, housing, and the rural community of South Royalton.

name: Washington and Lee University
description:
Washington and Lee University was founded in 1749. Being one of the smallest of the nation's top-tier law schools, Washington and Lee School of Law (W&L Law) is located in a college town in the majestic Shenandoah Valley of Virginia, a three-hour drive from Washington, DC and within an hour of several other metropolitan areas.
W&L Law has long been an innovator in legal education, and these innovations have allowed the school to build a singular community that educates students for character and challenges them to solve the problems they will face in a complex world. It fosters a desire not simply to act, but to act intelligently and ethically.

name: Yale University
description:
The Yale Graduate School of Arts and Sciences is one of fourteen schools composing
Yale University and the only one that awards the degrees of Doctor of Philosophy,
Master of Philosophy, Master of Arts, and Master of Science. The work of the
Graduate School is carried on in the divisions of the Humanities, Social Sciences, and
Biological and Physical Sciences. Fifty-six departments and programs offer courses of
study leading to the Ph.D. degree. There are nineteen programs that terminate with
the master’s degree.
Yale University comprises three major academic components: Yale College (the
undergraduate program), the Graduate School of Arts and Sciences, and the
professional schools. In addition, Yale encompasses a wide array of centers and
programs, libraries, museums, and administrative support offices. Approximately
11,250 students attend Yale.
